title.zh: 卷三百六十二 列傳第一百二十一 朱勝非 呂頤浩 范宗尹 范致虛 呂好問
title.en: Volume 362 Biographies 121: Zhu Shengfei, Lu Yihao, Fan Zongyin, Fan Zhixu, Lu Haowen
title.raw: 卷三百六十二 列傳第一百二十一 朱勝非 呂頤浩 范宗尹 范致虛 呂好問 Volume 362 Biographies 121: Zhu Shengfei, Lu Yihao, Fan Zongyin, Fan Zhixu, Lu Haowen

sentences.zh: 朱勝非 呂頤浩 范宗尹 范致虛 呂好問

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei, Lu Yihao, Fan Zongyin, Fan Zhixu, Lu Haowen
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei, Lu Yihao, Fan Zongyin, Fan Zhixu, and Lu Haowen

sentences.zh: 朱勝非

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei

sentences.zh: 二年，除尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was removed and appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign, he was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時宰執蔭補多濫，勝非奏：「舊制，宰執子弟例不堂除，只就銓注，罷政不以罪，然後推恩。

translations.literal: At the time, chief councillors' hereditary appointments were excessive and indiscriminate. Shengfei memorialized: "Under the old system, sons of chief councillors were by rule not given direct appointments from the hall; they only went through the regular selection process. After leaving office without being charged with a crime, favor was then extended.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, chief councillors were abusing hereditary appointments on a lavish scale. Shengfei submitted a memorial: "Under the old regulations, the sons of chief councillors were not ordinarily given direct appointments from court; they had to go through the regular selection process. Only after a councillor left office without being charged with a crime was favor then extended to his family.

sentences.zh: 趙普子弟皆作武臣，普再相，長子授莊宅使；

translations.literal: Zhao Pu's sons and younger brothers all became military officials. When Pu became chief councillor again, his eldest son was appointed Commissioner of the Imperial Manors;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu's sons and younger brothers all became military officials. When Pu returned as chief councillor, his eldest son was appointed Commissioner of the Imperial Manors;

sentences.zh: 范純仁再相，子正平有文行，竟死選調；

translations.literal: When Fan Chunren became chief councillor again, his son Zhengping had literary talent and conduct, yet in the end died while still in the selection process;
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chunren served again as chief councillor, his son Zhengping had both literary talent and moral conduct, yet in the end died still waiting in the appointment queue;

sentences.zh: 章惇子援及持皆高科，並為州縣、幕職、監當。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun's sons Yuan and Chi both passed with high examination ranks and all held posts as prefectural and county officials, staff assistants, and supervisory agents.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun's sons Yuan and Chi both earned top examination ranks and were all appointed to posts as prefectural and county officials, staff assistants, and supervisory agents.

sentences.zh: 惟夏竦子安期累作邊帥，授待制、直學士，王安石薦子雱為崇政殿說書，除待制。

translations.literal: Only Xia Song's son Anqi repeatedly served as frontier commander and was granted the titles of Attendant-in-Waiting and Academician Expositor; Wang Anshi recommended his son Bian as Lecturer at the Hall for Veneration of Governance and appointed him Attendant-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xia Song's son Anqi had repeatedly served as a frontier commander and was granted the titles of Attendant-in-Waiting and Academician Expositor; Wang Anshi recommended his son Bian as Lecturer at the Hall for Veneration of Governance and had him appointed Attendant-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 然安期猶有才幹，雱猶有學問。

translations.literal: Yet Anqi still had ability, and Bian still had learning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Anqi still had real ability, and Bian still had genuine learning.

sentences.zh: 至蔡京子六人、孫四人，鄭居中、劉正夫子各二人，余深、王黼、白時中、蔡卞、鄧洵仁洵武子各一人，並列從班。

translations.literal: By the time of Cai Jing, six sons and four grandsons, Zheng Juzhong and Liu Zhengfu each with two sons, Yu Shen, Wang Fu, Bai Shizhong, Cai Bian, and Deng Xunren and Xunwu each with one son, all ranked in the attendant class.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Cai Jing, six sons and four grandsons, Zheng Juzhong and Liu Zhengfu each with two sons, and Yu Shen, Wang Fu, Bai Shizhong, Cai Bian, and Deng Xunren and Xunwu each with one son—all were ranked in the attendant class.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，諫官疏謂：『尚從竹馬之遊，已造荷囊之列。』

translations.literal: At the end of the Xuanhe era, remonstrance officials submitted memorials saying: "They are still at the age of bamboo-horse play, yet already have entered the ranks of the purse-bearers."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xuanhe era, remonstrance officials submitted memorials saying: "They are still at the age of childhood play, yet already have entered the ranks of court attendants."

sentences.zh: 今不可以不戒。」

translations.literal: Now this must not go unheeded as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: This must not go unheeded as a warning now."

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，上自鎮江南幸，留勝非經理。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the emperor traveled south from Zhenjiang, Shengfei was left behind to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the emperor traveled south from Zhenjiang, Shengfei was left behind to manage affairs there.

sentences.zh: 未幾，命為控扼使，已而拜宣奉大夫、尚書右僕射兼禦營使。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed Control Commissioner; shortly thereafter he was invested as Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Imperial Camp Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was appointed Control Commissioner; shortly thereafter he was invested as Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently serving as Imperial Camp Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 故事，命相進三官，勝非特遷五官。

translations.literal: By precedent, appointing a chief councillor advanced rank by three grades; Shengfei was specially promoted by five grades.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, appointing a chief councillor advanced one's rank by three grades; Shengfei was specially promoted by five.

sentences.zh: 會王淵簽書樞密院事兼禦營司都統制，內侍復用事恣橫，諸將不悅。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Yuan was appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently served as overall commander of the Imperial Camp Office; eunuchs again wielded power arbitrarily, and the generals were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Wang Yuan was appointed to sign documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently served as overall commander of the Imperial Camp Office; eunuchs again wielded power arbitrarily, and the generals were displeased.

sentences.zh: 於是苗傅、劉正彥與其徒王鈞甫、馬柔吉、王世修謀，誣淵結宦官謀反。

translations.literal: Thereupon Miao Fu, Liu Zhengyan, and their followers Wang Junfu, Ma Rouji, and Wang Shixiu plotted, falsely accusing Yuan of conspiring with eunuchs to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Miao Fu, Liu Zhengyan, and their followers Wang Junfu, Ma Rouji, and Wang Shixiu plotted together, falsely accusing Yuan of conspiring with eunuchs to rebel.

sentences.zh: 正彥手斬淵，分捕中官，皆殺之，擁兵至行宮門外。

translations.literal: Zhengyan personally beheaded Yuan, sent parties to seize palace eunuchs, killed them all, and led troops to the gates outside the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan personally beheaded Yuan, sent parties to seize palace eunuchs and kill them all, and led troops to the gates outside the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 勝非趨樓上，詰專殺之由。

translations.literal: Shengfei hurried upstairs and questioned the reason for the unauthorized killing.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei hurried upstairs and demanded to know why they had carried out the killing on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 上親禦樓撫諭，傅、正彥語頗不遜，勝非乃從皇太后出諭旨。

translations.literal: The emperor personally went to the tower to console and instruct them; Fu and Zhengyan's words were quite disrespectful, so Shengfei then accompanied the Empress Dowager out to proclaim the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally went to the tower to console and instruct them; Fu and Zhengyan's words were quite disrespectful, so Shengfei then accompanied the Empress Dowager out to proclaim the imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 傅等請高宗避位，太后抱皇子聽政，太后不可。

translations.literal: Fu and the others requested that Emperor Gaozong step aside, that the Empress Dowager hold the infant prince and conduct government; the Empress Dowager would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and the others demanded that Emperor Gaozong step aside so the Empress Dowager could hold the infant prince and conduct government; the Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 傅顧勝非曰：「今日正須大臣果決，相公何無一言耶？」

translations.literal: Fu turned to Shengfei and said: "Today we truly need a chief minister who is resolute and decisive—why has the Chancellor not said a single word?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu turned to Shengfei and said: "Today we truly need a chief minister who is resolute and decisive—why has the Chancellor not said a single word?"

sentences.zh: 勝非還告上曰：「王鈞甫乃傅等腹心，適語臣云：『二將忠有餘，而學不足。』

translations.literal: Shengfei returned and reported to the emperor: "Wang Junfu is the trusted confidant of Fu and the others. He just told me, 'The two generals have loyalty to spare but learning in short supply.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei returned and reported to the emperor: "Wang Junfu is the trusted confidant of Fu and the others. He just told me, 'The two generals have loyalty to spare but learning in short supply.

sentences.zh: 此語可為後圖之緒。」

translations.literal: This remark can serve as a thread for later plans."
translations.idiomatic: This remark can serve as a thread for later plans."

sentences.zh: 於是太后垂簾，高宗退居顯忠寺，號睿聖宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Empress Dowager held court from behind the curtain, Gaozong withdrew to Xianzhong Temple, which was named Ruicheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Empress Dowager held court from behind the curtain, while Gaozong withdrew to Xianzhong Temple, which was renamed Ruicheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 勝非因請降赦以安傅等。

translations.literal: Shengfei thereupon requested an amnesty decree to reassure Fu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei thereupon requested an amnesty decree to reassure Fu and the others.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「母后垂簾，須二臣同對，此承平故事。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "When the Empress Mother holds court from behind the curtain, two ministers must jointly attend—this is the precedent of peaceful times.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "When the Empress Mother holds court from behind the curtain, two ministers must jointly attend—this is the precedent of peaceful times.

sentences.zh: 今日事機有須密奏者，乞許臣僚獨對，而日引傅徒二人上殿，以弭其疑。」

translations.literal: Today's situation has matters requiring confidential memorials; I beg that officials be permitted private audience, while daily summoning Fu's two followers to the hall to allay their suspicions."
translations.idiomatic: Today's situation has matters requiring confidential memorials; I beg that officials be permitted private audience, while daily summoning Fu's two followers to the hall to allay their suspicions."

sentences.zh: 太后語上曰：「賴相此人，若汪、黃在位，事已狼籍矣。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said to the emperor: "We depend on this Chancellor. Had Wang and Huang still been in office, affairs would already be in utter disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said to the emperor: "We depend on this Chancellor. Had Wang and Huang still been in office, affairs would already be in utter disorder."

sentences.zh: 王鈞甫見勝非，勝非問：「前言二將學不足，如何？」

translations.literal: Wang Junfu came to see Shengfei. Shengfei asked: "You said earlier that the two generals lack learning—what do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junfu came to see Shengfei. Shengfei asked: "You said earlier that the two generals lack learning—what do you mean by that?"

sentences.zh: 鈞甫曰：「如劉將手殺王淵，軍中亦非之。」

translations.literal: Junfu said: "For example, General Liu personally killed Wang Yuan—the army also disapproved of this."
translations.idiomatic: Junfu said: "For example, General Liu personally killed Wang Yuan—the army disapproved of that as well."

sentences.zh: 勝非因以言撼之曰：「上皇待燕士如骨肉，那無一人效力者乎？

translations.literal: Shengfei then used words to shake him, saying: "The Retired Emperor treated men of Yan like his own flesh and blood—could there not be a single one willing to serve?
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei then used words to shake him, saying: "The Retired Emperor treated men of Yan like his own flesh and blood—could there not be a single one willing to serve?

sentences.zh: 人言燕、趙多奇士，徒虛語耳。」

translations.literal: People say Yan and Zhao abound in extraordinary men—it is nothing but empty talk."
translations.idiomatic: People say Yan and Zhao abound in extraordinary men—it is nothing but empty talk."

sentences.zh: 鈞甫曰：「不可謂燕無人。」

translations.literal: Junfu said: "One cannot say Yan has no men."
translations.idiomatic: Junfu said: "One cannot say Yan has no capable men."

sentences.zh: 勝非曰：「君與馬參議皆燕中名人，嘗獻策滅契丹者。

translations.literal: Shengfei said: "You and Adviser Ma are both famous men of Yan who once submitted plans to destroy the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei said: "You and Adviser Ma are both famous men of Yan who once submitted plans to destroy the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 今金人所任，多契丹舊人，若渡江，禍首及君矣。

translations.literal: Now those the Jin employ are mostly former Khitan men. If they cross the Yangzi, the ringleaders will reach you.
translations.idiomatic: Now those the Jin employ are mostly former Khitan men. If they cross the Yangzi, the ringleaders will come for you.

sentences.zh: 盍早為朝廷協力乎！」

translations.literal: Why not early on exert yourselves for the court!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not exert yourselves for the court now, while there is still time!"

sentences.zh: 鈞甫唯唯。

translations.literal: Junfu assented repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Junfu assented repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 王世修來見，勝非諭之曰：「國家艱難，若等立功之秋也。

translations.literal: Wang Shixiu came to see him. Shengfei instructed him: "The state is in hardship—this is the season for men like you to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixiu came to see him. Shengfei instructed him: "The state is in hardship—this is the season for men like you to achieve merit.

sentences.zh: 誠能奮身立事，從官豈難得乎。」

translations.literal: If you truly throw yourselves into service and establish achievements, would attendant rank be hard to obtain?"
translations.idiomatic: If you truly throw yourselves into service and establish achievements, would attendant rank be hard to obtain?"

sentences.zh: 世修喜，時往來道軍中情實。

translations.literal: Shixiu was pleased and from time to time came and went, reporting the true situation in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu was pleased and from time to time came and went, reporting the true situation in the army.

sentences.zh: 擢世修為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shixiu was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiu was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 傅、正彥乞改年號及移蹕建康，勝非以白太后，因議恐盡廢其請，則倉卒變生，乃改元明受。

translations.literal: Fu and Zhengyan requested changing the reign title and moving the imperial residence to Jiankang. Shengfei reported this to the Empress Dowager. Because of discussion fearing that if all their requests were rejected, sudden change would arise, the era name was changed to Mingshou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Zhengyan requested changing the reign title and moving the imperial residence to Jiankang. Shengfei reported this to the Empress Dowager. Fearing that if all their requests were rejected, sudden upheaval would follow, the court changed the era name to Mingshou.

sentences.zh: 以詔示世修曰：「已從若請矣。」

translations.literal: He showed the edict to Shixiu and said: "Your request has already been granted."
translations.idiomatic: He showed the edict to Shixiu and said: "Your request has already been granted."

sentences.zh: 傅等欲挾上幸徽、越，勝非諭之以禍福而止。

translations.literal: Fu and the others wished to take the emperor to Huizhou and Yuezhou. Shengfei instructed them on fortune and misfortune and stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and the others wished to take the emperor to Huizhou and Yuezhou. Shengfei instructed them on the consequences and stopped them.

sentences.zh: 傅聞韓世忠起兵，取其妻子為質。

translations.literal: Fu heard that Han Shizhong had raised troops and took his wife and children as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu heard that Han Shizhong had raised troops, he took Han's wife and children as hostages.

sentences.zh: 勝非紿傅曰：「今當啟太后召二人慰撫，使報知平江，諸君益安。」

translations.literal: Shengfei deceived Fu, saying: "Now we should inform the Empress Dowager to summon the two men for consolation and have them report to Pingjiang—you gentlemen will be all the more secure."
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei deceived Fu, saying: "Now we should inform the Empress Dowager to summon the two men for consolation and have them report to Pingjiang—you gentlemen will be all the more secure."

sentences.zh: 傅許諾。

translations.literal: Fu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu agreed.

sentences.zh: 勝非喜曰：「二凶真無能為也。」

translations.literal: Shengfei rejoiced and said: "The two villains truly cannot accomplish anything."
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei rejoiced and said: "The two villains truly cannot accomplish anything."

sentences.zh: 諸將將至，傅等懼，勝非因謂之曰：「勤王之師未進者，使是間自反正耳。

translations.literal: The generals were about to arrive; Fu and the others were afraid. Shengfei therefore said to them: "As for the armies coming to rescue the throne that have not yet advanced—let this interval be used for you to correct yourselves on your own.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were about to arrive, and Fu and the others were afraid. Shengfei therefore said to them: "As for the armies coming to rescue the throne that have not yet advanced—use this interval to correct yourselves on your own.

sentences.zh: 不然，下詔率百官六軍請上還宮，公等置身何地乎？」

translations.literal: Otherwise, an edict will be issued leading the hundred officials and the Six Armies to request the emperor's return to the palace—where will you gentlemen place yourselves?"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, an edict will be issued leading the hundred officials and the Six Armies to request the emperor's return to the palace—where will you gentlemen place yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 即召學士李邴、張守作百官章及太后手詔。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned Academicians Li Bing and Zhang Shou to draft the memorial of the hundred officials and the Empress Dowager's handwritten edict.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately summoned Academicians Li Bing and Zhang Shou to draft the memorial of the hundred officials and the Empress Dowager's handwritten edict.

sentences.zh: 四月朔，勝非率百官詣睿聖宮，親掖上乘馬還宮。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, Shengfei led the hundred officials to Ruicheng Palace, personally supporting the emperor as he mounted his horse and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month, Shengfei led the hundred officials to Ruicheng Palace, personally supporting the emperor as he mounted his horse and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 苗傅請以王世修為參議，勝非曰：「世修已為從官，豈可復從軍？」

translations.literal: Miao Fu requested that Wang Shixiu serve as adviser. Shengfei said: "Shixiu is already an attendant official—how can he again follow the army?"
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu requested that Wang Shixiu serve as adviser. Shengfei said: "Shixiu is already an attendant official—how can he again follow the army?"

sentences.zh: 上既復辟，勝非曰：「臣昔遇變，義當即死，偷生至此，欲圖今日之事耳。」

translations.literal: After the emperor had been restored, Shengfei said: "When I formerly encountered the upheaval, by right I should have died at once. I stole life to reach this point only to plan for today's affair."
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor had been restored, Shengfei said: "When I formerly encountered the upheaval, by right I should have died at once. I stole life to reach this point only to plan for today's affair."

sentences.zh: 乃乞罷政。

translations.literal: He then requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested to leave office.

sentences.zh: 上問誰可代者，勝非曰：「呂頤浩、張浚。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked who could replace him. Shengfei said: "Lu Yihao and Zhang Jun."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked who could replace him. Shengfei said: "Lu Yihao and Zhang Jun."

sentences.zh: 問孰優，曰：「頤浩練事而暴，浚喜事而疏。」

translations.literal: Asked which was superior, he said: "Yihao is experienced in affairs but violent; Jun is eager for achievement but careless."
translations.idiomatic: Asked which was superior, he said: "Yihao is experienced in affairs but violent; Jun is eager for achievement but careless."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「浚太年少。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jun is too young."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Jun is too young."

sentences.zh: 勝非曰：「臣向被召，軍旅錢谷悉付浚，此舉浚實主之。」

translations.literal: Shengfei said: "When I was formerly summoned, military affairs and revenue grain were all entrusted to Jun; this undertaking Jun truly led."
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei said: "When I was formerly summoned, military affairs and revenue grain were all entrusted to Jun; this undertaking Jun truly led."

sentences.zh: 御史中丞張守論勝非不能預防，致賊猖獗，宜罷。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Shou argued that Shengfei could not take preventive measures, causing the rebels to run rampant, and that he should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Shou argued that Shengfei had failed to take preventive measures, allowing the rebels to run rampant, and that he should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 授觀文殿大學士、知洪州，尋除江西安撫大使兼知江州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Prefect of Hongzhou; shortly thereafter he was made Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner, concurrently Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Prefect of Hongzhou; shortly thereafter he was made Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner, concurrently serving as Prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，馬進陷江州，侍御史沈與求論九江之陷，由勝非赴鎮太緩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, Ma Jin captured Jiangzhou. Remonstrance Official Shen Yuqiu argued that the fall of Jiujiang was because Shengfei went to his post too slowly.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing, Ma Jin captured Jiangzhou. Remonstrance Official Shen Yuqiu argued that the fall of Jiujiang was because Shengfei had gone to his post too slowly.

sentences.zh: 降授中大夫，分司南京，江州居住。

translations.literal: His rank was reduced to Grand Master of Palace Attendance, assigned to nominal duty at the Southern Capital, residing at Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was reduced to Grand Master of Palace Attendance, assigned to nominal duty at the Southern Capital, and ordered to reside at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，呂頤浩薦兼侍讀，又薦都督江、淮、荊、浙諸軍事，給事中胡安國、侍御史江躋交章論罷之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Lu Yihao recommended him as concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting, and again recommended him as Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe; Supervising Secretary Hu Anguo and Remonstrance Official Jiang Ji submitted successive memorials arguing for his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Lu Yihao recommended him as concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting, and again recommended him as Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe; Supervising Secretary Hu Anguo and Remonstrance Official Jiang Ji submitted successive memorials arguing for his dismissal.

sentences.zh: 頤浩力引其入，再除兼侍讀，尋拜尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Yihao strongly brought him in; he was again appointed concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting, and shortly thereafter invested as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Chief Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao strongly brought him back; he was again appointed concurrent Lecturer-in-Waiting, and shortly thereafter invested as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Chief Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去，起復右僕射兼知樞密院事，上《吏部七司敕令格式》一百八十卷。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother, then was recalled from mourning as Right Vice Director, concurrently managing Bureau of Military Affairs affairs, and submitted the Statutes and Formats of the Seven Bureaus of the Ministry of Personnel in one hundred eighty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother, then was recalled from mourning as Right Vice Director, concurrently managing Bureau of Military Affairs affairs, and submitted the Statutes and Formats of the Seven Bureaus of the Ministry of Personnel in one hundred eighty juan.

sentences.zh: 時員外郎江端友請營宗廟，議者非之，以為國家期於恢復，不常厥居，勝非方主和議，遂白上營宗廟于臨安。

translations.literal: At the time, Vice Director Jiang Duanyou requested building an ancestral temple. Discussants opposed it, holding that the state looked to recovery and would not long remain in one place. Shengfei was then advocating peace talks and reported to the emperor to build the ancestral temple at Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Vice Director Jiang Duanyou requested building an ancestral temple. Critics opposed it, holding that the state looked to recovery and would not long remain in one place. Shengfei was then advocating peace talks and reported to the emperor to build the ancestral temple at Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 徐俯罷參政，勝非薦胡松年。

translations.literal: Xu Fu was dismissed from participating in government; Shengfei recommended Hu Songnian.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Fu was dismissed from participating in government, Shengfei recommended Hu Songnian.

sentences.zh: 侍御史常同劾松年乃王黼客，勝非徙同左史。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Chang Tong impeached Songnian as a client of Wang Fu. Shengfei transferred Tong to Left Historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Chang Tong impeached Songnian as a client of Wang Fu. Shengfei transferred Tong to Left Historiographer.

sentences.zh: 莫儔謫曲江，其家蒼頭奴為勝非治疽而愈，奴為儔請，得復官。

translations.literal: Mo Chou was banished to Qujiang. A bondservant in his household treated an abscess for Shengfei and cured it; the bondservant pleaded for Chou and he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Chou was banished to Qujiang. A bondservant in his household treated an abscess for Shengfei and cured it; the bondservant pleaded for Chou, and he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 姻家劉式嘗言為兵官獲盜，勝非不以付部用，特旨改官。

translations.literal: His affinal relative Liu Shi once reported that as a military officer he had captured bandits. Shengfei did not refer it to the ministry for appointment but used a special edict to change his rank.
translations.idiomatic: His affinal relative Liu Shi once reported that as a military officer he had captured bandits. Shengfei did not refer it to the ministry for appointment but used a special edict to change his rank.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，勝非累章乞免，且自論當罷者十一事。

translations.literal: When prolonged rain occurred, Shengfei submitted repeated memorials requesting dismissal, and himself set forth eleven matters for which he ought to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: When prolonged rain occurred, Shengfei submitted repeated memorials requesting dismissal, and himself set forth eleven matters for which he ought to be removed.

sentences.zh: 魏矼亦劾其罪，遂罷。

translations.literal: Wei Jiang also impeached his offenses, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiang also impeached his offenses, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 五年，慶詔言戰守四事，起知湖州，引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on a celebratory edict discussing four matters of war and defense, he was recalled to serve as Prefect of Huzhou, then cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on a celebratory edict discussing four matters of war and defense, he was recalled to serve as Prefect of Huzhou, then cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 勝非與秦檜有隙，檜得政，勝非廢居八年，卒，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: Shengfei had a rift with Qin Hui. When Hui gained power, Shengfei lived in retirement for eight years, then died. His posthumous title was Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei had a rift with Qin Hui. When Hui gained power, Shengfei lived in retirement for eight years, then died. He was given the posthumous title Zhongjing.

sentences.zh: 勝非，張邦昌友婿也。

translations.literal: Shengfei was the son-in-law of Zhang Bangchang's friend.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei was the son-in-law of Zhang Bangchang's friend.

sentences.zh: 始，邦昌僭位，勝非嘗械其使，及金人過江，勝非請尊禮邦昌，錄其後以謝敵。

translations.literal: At first, when Bangchang usurped the throne, Shengfei once shackled his envoys. When the Jin people crossed the Yangzi, Shengfei requested honoring Bangchang and recording his descendants to appease the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Bangchang usurped the throne, Shengfei once shackled his envoys. When the Jin crossed the Yangzi, Shengfei requested honoring Bangchang and recording his descendants to appease the enemy.

sentences.zh: 苗、劉之變，保護聖躬，功居多。

translations.literal: In the Miao and Liu upheaval, protecting the sacred person—his merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In the Miao and Liu upheaval, his merit in protecting the emperor's person was greatest.

sentences.zh: 既去，力薦張浚。

translations.literal: After he left office, he strongly recommended Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office, he strongly recommended Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 然李綱罷，勝非受黃潛善風旨草制，極言其狂妄。

translations.literal: Yet when Li Gang was dismissed, Shengfei received Huang Qianshan's intent and drafted the edict, speaking extremely of his arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Li Gang was dismissed, Shengfei received Huang Qianshan's intent and drafted the edict, speaking in the strongest terms of his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 再相，忌趙鼎，鼎宣撫川、陝，欲重使名以制吳玠，勝非曰：「元樞出使，豈論此耶？」

translations.literal: When he became chief councillor again, he was jealous of Zhao Ding. Ding was Pacification Commissioner of Sichuan and Shaanxi and wished to enhance his envoy title to control Wu Jie. Shengfei said: "When the Chief Councillor goes on mission, is this matter under discussion?"
translations.idiomatic: When he became chief councillor again, he was jealous of Zhao Ding. Ding was Pacification Commissioner of Sichuan and Shaanxi and wished to enhance his envoy title to control Wu Jie. Shengfei said: "When the Chief Councillor goes on mission, is this matter under discussion?"

sentences.zh: 蓋因事出鼎而輕其權。

translations.literal: This was because he used the matter to remove Ding and diminish his authority.
translations.idiomatic: This was because he used the matter to remove Ding and diminish his authority.

sentences.zh: 人以此少之。

translations.literal: People for this reason thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: People for this reason thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 及著《閒居錄》，亦多其私說云。

translations.literal: When he wrote Records of Secluded Living, it also contained much of his private opinions.
translations.idiomatic: When he wrote Records of Secluded Living, it also contained much of his private opinions.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩

translations.literal: Lu Yihao
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yihao

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩，字元直，其先樂陵人，徙齊州。

translations.literal: Lu Yihao, style name Yuanzhi, his ancestors were men of Leling, later moved to Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yihao, style name Yuanzhi, was descended from men of Leling who later moved to Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 中進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 父喪家貧，躬耕以贍老幼。

translations.literal: When his father died the family was poor; he personally plowed to support the old and young.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died the family was poor; he personally plowed the fields to support the old and young.

sentences.zh: 後為密州司戶參軍，以李清臣薦，為邠州教授。

translations.literal: Later he served as Revenue Clerk of Mizhou; on Li Qingchen's recommendation he became Instructor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Revenue Clerk of Mizhou; on Li Qingchen's recommendation he became Instructor of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 除宗子博士，累官入為太府少卿、直龍圖閣、河北轉運副使，升待制徽猷閣、都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Clan, and through successive offices entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall, and Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei; he was promoted to Attendant-in-Waiting of the Hall of Splendid Learning and Overall Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Erudite of the Imperial Clan, and through successive offices entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall, and Vice Transport Commissioner of Hebei; he was promoted to Attendant-in-Waiting of the Hall of Splendid Learning and Overall Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 伐燕之役，頤浩以轉輸隨種師道至白溝。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Yan, Yihao as transport commissioner followed Zhong Shidao to Baigou.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Yan, Yihao served as transport commissioner and followed Zhong Shidao to Baigou.

sentences.zh: 既得燕山，郭藥師眾二萬，契丹軍萬餘，皆仰給縣官，詔以頤浩為燕山府路轉運使。

translations.literal: After Yan Mountain was taken, Guo Yaoshi's force of twenty thousand and Khitan troops of more than ten thousand all depended on state provision; an edict appointed Yihao Transport Commissioner of the Yan Mountain Prefecture Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Mountain was taken, Guo Yaoshi's force of twenty thousand and Khitan troops of more than ten thousand all depended on state provision; an edict appointed Yihao Transport Commissioner of the Yan Mountain Prefecture Circuit.

sentences.zh: 頤浩奏：「開邊極遠，其勢難守，雖窮力竭財，無以善後。」

translations.literal: Yihao memorialized: "Opening the frontier to the farthest reaches—the situation is hard to defend. Even if we exhaust strength and drain wealth, there is no way to manage the aftermath."
translations.idiomatic: Yihao memorialized: "Opening the frontier to the farthest reaches—the situation is hard to defend. Even if we exhaust strength and drain wealth, there is no way to manage the aftermath."

sentences.zh: 又奏燕山、河北危急五事，願博議久長之策。

translations.literal: He also memorialized five urgent matters concerning Yan Mountain and Hebei, wishing for broad discussion of a long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized five urgent matters concerning Yan Mountain and Hebei, wishing for broad discussion of a long-term strategy.

sentences.zh: 徽宗怒，命褫職貶官，而領職如故；

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong was angry and ordered his office stripped and rank reduced, yet he continued in his post as before;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong was angry and ordered his office stripped and rank reduced, yet he continued in his post as before;

sentences.zh: 尋復焉。

translations.literal: before long it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: before long both were restored.

sentences.zh: 進徽猷閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician Expositor of the Hall of Splendid Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Academician Expositor of the Hall of Splendid Learning.

sentences.zh: 金人入燕，郭藥師劫頤浩與蔡靖等以降。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens entered Yan, Guo Yaoshi seized Yihao and Cai Jing and others to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens took Yan, Guo Yaoshi captured Yihao, Cai Jing, and others and forced them to surrender.

sentences.zh: 敵退得歸，復以為河北都轉運使，以病辭，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: After the enemy withdrew he was able to return; he was again appointed Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei, declined on grounds of illness, and was made Supervisor of the Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew he made his way home and was reappointed Chief Transport Commissioner of Hebei, but he declined citing illness and accepted the post of Supervisor of the Chongfu Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，除知揚州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Yihao was appointed Prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Yihao was appointed prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕南幸，頤浩入見，除戶部侍郎兼知揚州，進戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured south, Yihao entered for audience; he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue concurrently Prefect of Yangzhou, and advanced to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved south, Yihao had an audience and was made Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrent prefect of Yangzhou, then promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 劇賊張遇眾數萬屯金山，縱兵焚掠。

translations.literal: The notorious bandit Zhang Yu, with a force of several tens of thousands, encamped at Jinshan and loosed his troops to burn and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The notorious rebel Zhang Yu led tens of thousands of men encamped at Jinshan, sending his troops out to burn and loot.

sentences.zh: 頤浩單騎與韓世忠造其壘，說之以逆順，遇黨釋甲降。

translations.literal: Yihao went alone on horseback with Han Shizhong to his camp, explained to them the difference between rebellion and loyalty, and Zhang Yu's followers laid down their armor and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao rode alone with Han Shizhong to the rebel camp and argued the right and wrong of their cause; Zhang Yu's followers thereupon disarmed and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，金人逼揚州，車駕南渡鎮江，召從臣問去留。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan, the Jurchens pressed Yangzhou; the imperial carriage crossed south to Zhenjiang; the emperor summoned his followers and asked whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan (1128), as Jurchen forces closed on Yangzhou, the emperor crossed the Yangtze to Zhenjiang and summoned his ministers to ask whether they should remain or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 頤浩叩頭願且留此，為江北聲援；

translations.literal: Yihao kowtowed and wished to remain here for the time being as a supporting force north of the river;
translations.idiomatic: Yihao kowtowed and urged that they stay put for now to maintain a hold in the north and keep pressure on the enemy from across the river;

sentences.zh: 不然，敵乘勢渡江，事愈急矣。

translations.literal: otherwise, if the enemy seized the momentum to cross the river, affairs would grow ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the enemy would ride their momentum across the Yangtze and the crisis would only worsen.

sentences.zh: 駕幸錢塘，拜同簽書樞密院事、江淮兩浙制置使，還屯京口。

translations.literal: When the carriage reached Qiantang, he was appointed Co-signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Commissioner for Jianghuai and Liang-Zhe, and returned to encamp at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Qiantang, he was appointed Co-signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Commissioner for Jianghuai and Liang-Zhe, then withdrew to encamp at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 金人去揚州，改江東安撫、制置使兼知江寧府。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens left Yangzhou, his post was changed to Jiangdong Pacification and Military Affairs Commissioner concurrently Prefect of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens withdrew from Yangzhou, he was reassigned as Jiangdong Pacification and Military Affairs Commissioner and concurrent prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 時苗傅、劉正彥為逆，逼高宗避位。

translations.literal: At that time Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled and forced Emperor Gaozong to step aside from the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rose in rebellion and compelled Emperor Gaozong to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 頤浩至江寧，奉明受改元詔赦，會監司議，皆莫敢對。

translations.literal: When Yihao reached Jiangning, he received the pardon edict announcing the change of era name to Mingshou; he convened the supervisory officials to discuss it, and none dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Yihao arrived at Jiangning, he received the pardon edict announcing the new reign title Mingshou and convened the circuit supervisors to discuss it—but none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 頤浩曰：「是必有兵變。」

translations.literal: Yihao said: "This must certainly be a military mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: Yihao said, "There must have been a military mutiny."

sentences.zh: 其子抗曰：「主上春秋鼎盛，二帝蒙塵沙漠，日望拯救，其肯遽遜位於幼沖乎？

translations.literal: His son Kang said: "Our lord's years are in full vigor; the two emperors suffer in the desert sands and look daily for deliverance—how could he willingly abdicate in favor of one so young and immature?
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang said, "The emperor is in the prime of life; the two captive emperors languish in the desert, and the court daily awaits their rescue—would he truly step aside so hastily for a child?

sentences.zh: 灼知兵變無疑也。」

translations.literal: One can know with certainty that a military mutiny is beyond doubt."
translations.idiomatic: It is unmistakably a mutiny."

sentences.zh: 頤浩即遣人寓書張浚曰：「時事如此，吾儕可但已乎？」

translations.literal: Yihao immediately sent someone with a letter to Zhang Jun saying: "Affairs are as they are—can we fellows simply let matters rest?"
translations.idiomatic: Yihao immediately sent Zhang Jun a letter asking, "Affairs have come to this—can men like us simply do nothing?

sentences.zh: 浚亦謂頤浩有威望，能斷大事，書來報起兵狀。

translations.literal: Jun also considered that Yihao had prestige and could decide great affairs; a letter came reporting the situation of raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, for his part, regarded Yihao as a figure of authority capable of decisive action, and wrote back with word that he was mobilizing.

sentences.zh: 頤浩乃與浚及諸將約，會兵討賊。

translations.literal: Yihao then joined Jun and the generals in an agreement to assemble troops and punish the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao then joined Jun and the other generals in a pact to converge their forces and crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時江寧士民洶懼，頤浩乃檄楊惟忠留屯，以安人心。

translations.literal: At that time the people and soldiers of Jiangning were greatly fearful; Yihao issued an order for Yang Weizhong to remain encamped there to settle people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: With the people of Jiangning in uproar, Yihao ordered Yang Weizhong to hold his position in the city to steady public morale.

sentences.zh: 且恐苗傅等計窮挾帝繇廣德渡江，戒惟忠先為控扼備。

translations.literal: Moreover, fearing that Miao Fu and the others, their plans exhausted, might seize the emperor and cross the river by way of Guangde, he warned Weizhong to prepare controls and defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared that Miao Fu's faction, driven to desperation, might seize the emperor and flee across the river via Guangde, and so warned Weizhong to secure the crossing in advance.

sentences.zh: 俄有旨，召頤浩赴院供職。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict arrived summoning Yihao to the Bureau to perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an imperial order summoned Yihao back to the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上言：「今金人乘戰勝之威，群盜有蜂起之勢，興衰撥亂，事屬艱難，豈容皇帝退享安逸？

translations.literal: He submitted: "Now the Jurchens ride the momentum of battle victory; bandits everywhere threaten to swarm up; to restore the dynasty and suppress disorder—the matter is grievously difficult—how can the emperor withdraw to enjoy ease and comfort?
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The Jurchens are riding high on victory, rebels are gathering like swarming bees, and the task of reviving the dynasty amid chaos could hardly be more arduous—how can the emperor retire to ease and comfort?

sentences.zh: 請亟復明辟，以圖恢復。」

translations.literal: I ask that the legitimate ruler be quickly restored, to plan for recovery."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the rightful sovereign be restored at once so that we may pursue national recovery."

sentences.zh: 遂以兵發江寧，舉鞭誓眾，士皆感厲＃

translations.literal: He then set out with troops from Jiangning, raised his whip and swore an oath to the multitude, and the soldiers were all stirred and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched out of Jiangning at the head of his army, raised his whip and pledged his oath before the assembled troops, and every man was stirred to fervor.

sentences.zh: 將至平江，張浚乘輕舟迓之，相持而泣，咨以大計。

translations.literal: As he was about to reach Pingjiang, Zhang Jun took a light boat to welcome him; they embraced and wept, and consulted on the grand plan.
translations.idiomatic: Near Pingjiang, Zhang Jun met him in a light skiff; the two clasped each other in tears and laid out their overall strategy.

sentences.zh: 頤浩曰：「頤浩曩諫開邊，幾死宦臣之手；

translations.literal: Yihao said: "Yihao once remonstrated against opening the frontier and nearly died at the hands of palace eunuchs;
translations.idiomatic: Yihao said, "I once warned against opening the frontier and nearly perished at the hands of palace eunuchs;

sentences.zh: 承乏漕挽，幾陷腥膻之域。

translations.literal: I took on the burdensome post of grain transport and nearly fell into the barbarian meat-eating lands.
translations.idiomatic: I then took charge of grain transport and nearly fell into enemy hands on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 今事不諧，不過赤族，為社稷死，豈不快乎？」

translations.literal: If today's affair does not succeed, it is no more than extermination of my whole clan—to die for the altars of state, is that not satisfying?"
translations.idiomatic: If we fail now, the worst that awaits is the annihilation of my clan—what happier end than to die for the realm?

sentences.zh: 浚壯其言。

translations.literal: Jun admired his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was heartened by his resolve.

sentences.zh: 即舟中草檄，進韓世忠為前軍，張俊翼之，劉光世為遊擊，頤浩、浚總中軍，光世分軍殿後。

translations.literal: He immediately drafted a proclamation aboard the boat, advancing Han Shizhong as vanguard, Zhang Jun to flank him, Liu Guangshi as mobile striker, Yihao and Jun to command the center army, with Guangshi dividing his force as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: On the spot he drafted a proclamation aboard the boat: Han Shizhong would lead the vanguard, Zhang Jun would cover his flank, Liu Guangshi would serve as mobile striker, Yihao and Jun would command the center, and Guangshi would bring up the rear with a detached force.

sentences.zh: 頤浩發平江，傅黨托旨請頤浩單騎入朝。

translations.literal: When Yihao set out from Pingjiang, Fu's faction, using a supposed imperial order, requested that Yihao enter court alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: As Yihao marched from Pingjiang, Miao Fu's faction sent word—in the emperor's name—asking him to ride in alone.

sentences.zh: 頤浩奏所統將士，忠義所激，可合不可離。

translations.literal: Yihao submitted that the officers and soldiers under his command, stirred by loyalty and righteousness, could be united but not separated.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao replied that the troops under his command, fired by loyalty and righteousness, could stand together but must not be split apart.

sentences.zh: 傅等恐懼，乃請高宗復辟。

translations.literal: Fu and the others grew fearful and thereupon requested that Emperor Gaozong be restored to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu and his allies, alarmed, then petitioned for Emperor Gaozong's restoration.

sentences.zh: 師次秀州，頤浩勉勵諸將曰：「今雖反正，而賊猶握兵居內。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Xiuzhou, Yihao exhorted the generals, saying: "Though we have now returned to righteousness, the rebels still hold troops within.
translations.idiomatic: When the army encamped at Xiuzhou, Yihao urged his commanders: "Although the emperor has been restored, the rebels still hold their arms inside the capital.

sentences.zh: 事若不濟，必反以惡名加我，翟義、徐敬業可監也。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, they will surely turn evil names against us—Zhai Yi and Xu Jingye can serve as warnings."
translations.idiomatic: If we fail, they will turn the blame on us as traitors—let Zhai Yi and Xu Jingye be our warning."

sentences.zh: 次臨平，苗傅等拒戰。

translations.literal: Next they reached Linping; Miao Fu and the others resisted in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Linping, Miao Fu and his allies offered battle.

sentences.zh: 頤浩被甲立水次，出入行陣，督世忠等破賊，傅、正彥引兵遁。

translations.literal: Yihao donned armor and stood by the water's edge, going in and out of the battle lines, supervising Han Shizhong and the others in breaking the rebels; Fu and Zhengyan led their troops in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao donned armor and took his stand on the riverbank, moving through the ranks to direct Han Shizhong and the others in crushing the rebels; Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan fled with their troops.

sentences.zh: 頤浩等以勤王兵入城，都人夾道聳觀，以手加額。

translations.literal: Yihao and the others entered the city with the troops who had come to rescue the emperor; the capital people lined the roads to watch in astonishment and placed their hands on their foreheads.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao and his army entered the capital as deliverers; townspeople lined the streets in wonder, their hands pressed to their brows in relief.

sentences.zh: 朱勝非罷相，以頤浩守尚書右僕射、中書侍郎兼禦營使，改同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei was dismissed as chief councilor; Yihao was appointed to hold the posts of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Commissioner of the Imperial Camp, and was changed to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shengfei was removed as chief councilor, Yihao was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Commissioner of the Imperial Camp, and elevated to Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸建康，聞金人復入，召諸將問移蹕之地，頤浩曰：「金人謀以陛下所至為邊面，今當且戰且避，奉陛下于萬全之地，臣願留常、潤死守。」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Jiankang and word came that the Jurchens had entered again, the emperor summoned the generals to ask where to move the imperial seat; Yihao said: "The Jurchens intend to treat wherever Your Majesty goes as the frontier line; now we should fight while retreating and escort Your Majesty to a place of complete safety—I wish to remain at Chang and Run to defend to the death."
translations.idiomatic: When the court reached Jiankang and word came that the Jurchens had crossed in again, the emperor asked his generals where to relocate the court. Yihao said, "The enemy means to turn wherever Your Majesty goes into the front line. We must fight as we withdraw and conduct Your Majesty to safety. I myself will stay behind at Changzhou and Runzhou and hold them to the death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕左右不可以無相。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "At my side there cannot be no chief councilor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I cannot be without a chief councilor at my side.

sentences.zh: 乃以韓世忠守鎮江，劉光世守太平。

translations.literal: Thereupon Han Shizhong was assigned to guard Zhenjiang and Liu Guangshi to guard Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong was ordered to hold Zhenjiang and Liu Guangshi Taiping.

sentences.zh: 駕至平江，聞杜充敗績，上曰：「事迫矣，若何？」

translations.literal: When the carriage reached Pingjiang and word came of Du Chong's defeat, the emperor said: "Affairs are pressing—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: When the court reached Pingjiang and news arrived of Du Chong's rout, the emperor said, "The crisis is upon us—what are we to do?

sentences.zh: 頤浩遂進航海之策。

translations.literal: Yihao thereupon advanced the plan of taking to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao then proposed fleeing by sea.

sentences.zh: 初，建炎禦營使本以行幸總齊軍政，而宰相兼領之，遂專兵柄，樞府幾無所預。

translations.literal: Initially, the Jianyan Imperial Camp Commissioner was originally meant to oversee all military affairs during the imperial tour, but because the chief councilor concurrently held the post, military authority became monopolized and the Bureau of Military Affairs was scarcely involved.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the Imperial Camp Commissioner was created to centralize military affairs during the imperial flight; but because the chief councilor also held the post, he monopolized command and the Bureau of Military Affairs was left with almost nothing to do.

sentences.zh: 頤浩在位尤顓恣，趙鼎論其過。

translations.literal: While in office Yihao was especially autocratic and willful; Zhao Ding criticized his faults.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yihao was especially high-handed and domineering, and Zhao Ding denounced his abuses.

sentences.zh: 四年，移鼎為翰林學士、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Ding was transferred to Academician of the Hanlin Academy and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhao Ding was moved to Academician of the Hanlin Academy and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 鼎辭，且攻頤浩，章十數上，頤浩求去。

translations.literal: Ding declined and moreover attacked Yihao; memorials numbering more than ten were submitted; Yihao requested removal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding refused the appointment and launched a sustained attack on Yihao, submitting more than a dozen memorials; Yihao asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 除鎮南軍節度、開府儀同三司、醴泉觀使，詔以頤浩倡義勤王，故從優禮焉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, Commissioner with Ceremonial Parity of the Three Excellencies, and Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey; an edict stated that because Yihao had taken the lead in the righteous campaign to rescue the emperor, he was therefore accorded exceptional honors.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, Commissioner with Ceremonial Parity of the Three Excellencies, and Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey—the edict citing his leadership in the righteous campaign to rescue the emperor as grounds for the generous treatment.

sentences.zh: 奉化賊將璉乘亂為變，劫頤浩置軍中，高宗以頤浩故，赦而招之。

translations.literal: The Fenghua rebel general Lian seized the disorder to mutiny, seized Yihao and placed him in the army; Emperor Gaozong, on Yihao's account, pardoned and summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: The Fenghua rebel commander Lian exploited the chaos to revolt, seized Yihao, and held him in camp; for Yihao's sake the emperor pardoned the rebel and offered to take him back into service.

sentences.zh: 尋除江東安撫、制置大使兼知池州。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Jiangdong Pacification and Military Affairs Grand Commissioner concurrently Prefect of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Jiangdong Pacification and Military Affairs Grand Commissioner and concurrent prefect of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 頤浩請兵五萬屯建康等處，又請王?燮、巨師古兵自隸。

translations.literal: Yihao requested fifty thousand troops to encamp at Jiankang and other places, and also requested that the troops of Wang Xie and Ju Shigu be placed under his direct command.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao asked for fifty thousand men to garrison Jiankang and neighboring posts, and requested that the forces of Wang Xie and Ju Shigu be placed under his personal command.

sentences.zh: 將之鎮，而李成遣將馬進圍江州。

translations.literal: As he was about to go to his post, Li Cheng sent his general Ma Jin to besiege Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was setting out for his post, Li Cheng dispatched his general Ma Jin to besiege Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃駐軍鄱陽，會楊惟忠兵，請與俱趨南康，遣師古救江州。

translations.literal: He thereupon encamped his army at Poyang, joined Yang Weizhong's troops, requested to hurry together toward Nankang, and dispatched Shigu to relieve Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Poyang, combined forces with Yang Weizhong, asked to advance together on Nankang, and sent Ju Shigu to relieve Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊眾鏖戰，頤浩、惟忠失利，師古敗奔洪州。

translations.literal: The rebel host fought fiercely in close combat; Yihao and Weizhong suffered defeat; Shigu was defeated and fled to Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In fierce combat the rebels gained the upper hand—Yihao and Weizhong were beaten, and Ju Shigu was routed and fled to Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 頤浩乞濟師討李成，高宗曰：「頤浩奮不顧身，為國討賊，群臣所不及，但輕進，其失也。」

translations.literal: Yihao begged for reinforcing troops to punish Li Cheng; Emperor Gaozong said: "Yihao rushes forward without regard for his person and punishes rebels for the state—a thing the ministers cannot match—but his fault lies in advancing rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Yihao requested reinforcements to bring Li Cheng to heel. Emperor Gaozong said, "Yihao has thrown himself into the fight for the realm as no other minister has—but rash advance is his failing.

sentences.zh: 詔王?燮以萬人速往策應。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wang Xie to take ten thousand men and hurry to coordinate support.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Xie to march ten thousand men to his aid at once.

sentences.zh: 頤浩復軍左蠡，又得閣門舍人崔增之眾萬餘，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: Yihao reassembled his army at Zuoli, and also obtained more than ten thousand troops under Gatehouse Attendant Cui Zeng; the army's momentum was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao regrouped at Zuoli and picked up another ten thousand-odd men under the Gatehouse Attendant Cui Zeng, and his army's strength revived.

sentences.zh: 命?燮、增擊賊，敗之，乘勝至江州，則馬進已陷城矣。

translations.literal: He ordered Xie and Zeng to strike the rebels and defeated them; riding the victory to Jiangzhou, Ma Jin had already taken the city.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Xie and Cui Zeng against the rebels and routed them, but when they pressed on to Jiangzhou they found Ma Jin had already taken the city.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命張俊為招討使，俊既至，遂敗馬進。

translations.literal: The court appointed Zhang Jun Pacification Commissioner; once Jun arrived, Ma Jin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Zhang Jun pacification commissioner; when he arrived he routed Ma Jin.

sentences.zh: 進遁，成以余眾降劉豫。

translations.literal: Jin fled; Cheng surrendered his remaining troops to Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jin fled, and Li Cheng surrendered his remaining forces to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 詔以淮南民未復業，須威望大臣措置，以頤浩兼宣撫，領壽春府、徐廬和州、無為軍。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because the people of Huainan had not yet resumed their livelihoods, a prestigious senior minister was needed to manage affairs; Yihao was concurrently made Pacification Commissioner, overseeing Shouchun Prefecture, Xu, Lu, Hezhou, and the Wuwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict held that Huainan needed a minister of standing to set affairs in order, and made Yihao Pacification Commissioner with authority over Shouchun, Xu, Lu, Hezhou, and the Wuwei Army.

sentences.zh: 招降趙延壽于分寧，得其精銳五千，分隸諸將。

translations.literal: He induced Zhao Yanshou to surrender at Fening and obtained five thousand elite troops, distributing them among the various generals.
translations.idiomatic: At Fening he persuaded Zhao Yanshou to defect, took five thousand picked troops from him, and distributed them among his commanders.

sentences.zh: 張琪自徽犯饒州，有眾五萬。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi from Huizhou invaded Raozhou with a force of fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi marched from Huizhou against Raozhou at the head of fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 時頤浩自左蠡班師，帳下兵不滿萬人，郡人惶駭。

translations.literal: At that time Yihao was returning his army from Zuoli; the troops under his banner numbered fewer than ten thousand; the people of the prefecture were terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao was then withdrawing from Zuoli with fewer than ten thousand men under his banner, and the people of the prefecture were panic-stricken.

sentences.zh: 頤浩命其將閻皋、姚端、崔邦弼列陣以待。

translations.literal: Yihao ordered his generals Yan Gao, Yao Duan, and Cui Bangbi to deploy battle formations and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao ordered his generals Yan Gao, Yao Duan, and Cui Bangbi to draw up in battle order and stand ready.

sentences.zh: 琪犯皋軍，皋力戰，端、邦弼兩軍夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Qi attacked Gao's army; Gao fought fiercely; Duan's and Bangbi's two armies struck from both flanks and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi hit Yan Gao's line; Gao fought hard while Yao Duan and Cui Bangbi struck from both sides and shattered the enemy.

sentences.zh: 拜少保、尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事兼知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Guardian, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Councilor, and concurrently Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Guardian, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Councilor, and concurrently director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，上自越州還臨安。

translations.literal: In the second year, the emperor returned from Yuezhou to Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of his reign the emperor returned from Yuezhou to Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 時桑仲在襄陽，欲進取京城，乞朝廷舉兵為聲援。

translations.literal: At that time Sang Zhong was at Xiangyang and wished to advance and take the capital city; he begged the court to raise troops as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Zhong was then at Xiangyang, planning a push on the old capital, and asked the court for troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 頤浩乃大議出師，而身自督軍北向。

translations.literal: Yihao thereupon held broad discussions on sending out troops and personally supervised the army northward.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao launched a major debate over taking the field and personally directed the northern advance.

sentences.zh: 高宗諭頤浩、秦檜曰：「頤浩治軍旋，檜理庶務，如種、蠡分職可也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong instructed Yihao and Qin Hui, saying: "Let Yihao manage the army's return, Hui handle routine affairs—like Wen and Fan dividing their duties, this will do."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong told Yihao and Qin Hui, "Let Yihao oversee the military withdrawal and Hui manage civil affairs—as when Wen and Fan divided their roles, that will suffice.

sentences.zh: 二人同秉政，檜知頤浩不為公論所與，多引知名士為助，欲傾之而擅朝權。

translations.literal: The two men held power together; Hui knew that Yihao did not enjoy public opinion's support and drew in many well-known scholar-officials as helpers, wishing to overturn him and monopolize court authority.
translations.idiomatic: The two shared power, but Qin Hui knew Yihao lacked public support and recruited prominent scholars to bolster himself, aiming to oust Yihao and seize control of the court.

sentences.zh: 高宗乃下詔以戒朋黨，除頤浩都督江、淮、荊、浙諸軍事，開府鎮江。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong thereupon issued an edict warning against factional cliques, appointed Yihao Grand Commander of military affairs for Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe, and opened an headquarters at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict warning against factionalism, made Yihao grand commander of all military affairs in the Jiang, Huai, Jing, and Zhe regions, and established his headquarters at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 頤浩辟文武士七十余人，以神武後軍及御前忠銳崔增、趙延壽二軍從行，百官班送。

translations.literal: Yihao recruited more than seventy civil and military scholars, taking with him the Shenwu Rear Army and the two Imperial Front Loyal Elite armies of Cui Zeng and Zhao Yanshou; officials of all ranks saw him off in procession.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao took on more than seventy civil and military advisers and set out with the Shenwu Rear Army and the Imperial Front Loyal Elite forces under Cui Zeng and Zhao Yanshou; the entire bureaucracy turned out to see him off.

sentences.zh: 頤浩次常州，延壽軍叛，劉光世殲其眾；

translations.literal: When Yihao halted at Changzhou, Yanshou's army mutinied; Liu Guangshi annihilated its force;
translations.idiomatic: At Changzhou, Zhao Yanshou's troops mutinied and Liu Guangshi wiped them out;

sentences.zh: 又聞桑仲已死，遂不進，引疾求罷。

translations.literal: moreover he heard that Sang Zhong was already dead; he therefore did not advance, cited illness, and requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: learning then that Sang Zhong was dead, he halted the advance, pleaded illness, and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 詔還朝，以知紹興府朱勝非同都督諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his return to court; Zhu Shengfei, Prefect of Shaoxing, was made Co-Grand Commander of all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and Zhu Shengfei, prefect of Shaoxing, was appointed co-commander of all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 頤浩既還，欲傾秦檜，乃引勝非為助。

translations.literal: After Yihao returned, wishing to overturn Qin Hui, he drew in Shengfei as help.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court, Yihao sought to bring down Qin Hui and enlisted Shengfei as an ally.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡安國論勝非必誤大計，勝非復知紹興府，尋以醴泉觀使兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Supervising Policy Adviser Hu Anguo argued that Shengfei would surely err in the great plan; Shengfei was again made Prefect of Shaoxing, and before long was made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey concurrently Court Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Policy Adviser Hu Anguo argued that Shengfei would ruin the grand strategy; Shengfei was sent back to govern Shaoxing and soon after made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey and concurrent court reader.

sentences.zh: 安國持錄黃不下，頤浩持命檢正諸房文字黃龜年書行。

translations.literal: Anguo held the recorded yellow document and would not transmit it downward; Yihao, holding an order, had the Reviser of Documents in the various offices Huang Guinian sign and issue it.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo withheld the draft edict; Yihao, invoking imperial authority, had the reviser of documents Huang Guinian sign and promulgate it.

sentences.zh: 安國以失職求去，罷之。

translations.literal: Anguo, on the grounds of having lost his post's function, requested removal; he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo, protesting that he had been stripped of his duties, asked to resign and was removed.

sentences.zh: 檜上章乞留安國，不報。

translations.literal: Hui submitted a memorial begging that Anguo be retained; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui memorialized asking that Hu Anguo be kept on; the emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 侍御史江躋、左司諫吳表臣皆以論救安國罷，程瑀、胡世將、劉一止、張燾、林待聘、樓炤亦坐論檜黨斥，台省一空，遂罷檜相。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Jiang Ji and Left Remonstrance Bureau Remonstrator Wu Biaochen were both dismissed for speaking in defense of Anguo; Cheng Yu, Hu Shijiang, Liu Yizhi, Zhang Tao, Lin Daipin, and Lou Zhao were also banished for criticizing Hui's faction; the censorate and remonstrance bureau were emptied; Hui was thereupon dismissed as chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Jiang Ji and Left Remonstrance Bureau Remonstrator Wu Biaochen were dismissed for defending Hu Anguo; Cheng Yu, Hu Shijiang, Liu Yizhi, Zhang Tao, Lin Daipin, and Lou Zhao were also ousted for attacking Qin Hui's faction; the censorate and remonstrance offices were emptied out, and Qin Hui was removed as chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 頤浩獨秉政，屢請興師復中原，謂：「太祖取天下，兵不過十萬，今有兵十六七萬矣。

translations.literal: Yihao alone held power and repeatedly requested raising troops to recover the Central Plain, saying: "When Taizu took the realm, troops numbered no more than one hundred thousand; now there are one hundred sixty or seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao held sole power and repeatedly urged marching north to recover the Central Plain, arguing: "When Taizu conquered the realm he fielded fewer than a hundred thousand men; today we have a hundred and sixty or seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 然自金人南牧，莫敢嬰其鋒。

translations.literal: Yet since the Jurchens drove south to pasture their herds, none dared touch their spear-points.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the Jurchens swept south, no one has dared meet them head-on.

sentences.zh: 比年韓世忠、張俊、陳思恭、張榮屢奏，人有戰心，天將悔禍。

translations.literal: In recent years Han Shizhong, Zhang Jun, Chen Sigong, and Zhang Rong have repeatedly memorialized; men have hearts for battle; Heaven will repent of the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Han Shizhong, Zhang Jun, Chen Sigong, and Zhang Rong have repeatedly urged action—the troops are ready to fight, and Heaven itself may be turning from disaster.

sentences.zh: 又金人以中原付劉豫，三尺童子知其不能立國。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Jurchens have entrusted the Central Plain to Liu Yu—even a three-foot child knows he cannot establish a state.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Jurchens have handed the Central Plain to Liu Yu; even a child knows that puppet regime cannot last.

sentences.zh: 願睿斷早定，決策北向。

translations.literal: I wish that sagely decision be settled early and a policy decided to face north.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will decide swiftly and commit to a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 今之精銳皆中原人，恐久而消磨，他日難以舉事。」

translations.literal: The elite troops now are all Central Plain people; I fear that over time they will be worn away and on another day it will be hard to undertake the affair."
translations.idiomatic: Our best troops are all northerners; if we wait too long their fighting spirit will fade and recovery will become far harder.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊稍息，頤浩請遣使循行郡國，平獄訟，宣德意。

translations.literal: At that time bandits had somewhat subsided; Yihao requested dispatching envoys to travel through the commanderies and states, settle prison cases and lawsuits, and spread imperial virtue and intent.
translations.idiomatic: With banditry finally easing, Yihao proposed sending envoys through the provinces to settle lawsuits and proclaim the emperor's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 李綱宣撫湖南，頤浩言綱縱暴無善狀，請罷諸路宣撫之名，綱止為安撫使。

translations.literal: Li Gang was grand pacification commissioner for Hunan; Yihao said Gang was indulgent and violent without good conduct, requested abolishing the grand pacification title on all circuits, and Gang was reduced to soothing commissioner only.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang was grand pacification commissioner for Hunan; Yihao charged that Gang had run wild without a single redeeming act, asked that the grand pacification title be abolished on every circuit, and reduced Gang to ordinary pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時李光在江東，與頤浩書，言綱有大節，四夷畏服。

translations.literal: At that time Li Guang was in Jiangdong and wrote to Yihao, saying Gang had great integrity and the four barbarians feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, then in Jiangdong, wrote to Yihao praising Li Gang's moral stature and arguing that even foreign peoples respected him.

sentences.zh: 頤浩稱光結黨，言者因論光，罷之。

translations.literal: Yihao called Guang a faction-maker; remonstrators therefore criticized Guang and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao accused Li Guang of factionalism; his critics took the cue and Li Guang was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 時方審量濫賞，頤浩時有縱舍，右司郎官王岡持不可，曰：「公秉國鈞，不平謂何。」

translations.literal: At that time they were reviewing excessive rewards; Yihao at times showed leniency in release; Right Department Bureau Langguan Wang Gang held that this would not do, saying: "Your Excellency holds the nation's scale—if not even-handed, what does that signify?"
translations.idiomatic: The court was reviewing excessive enfeoffments and rewards; Yihao sometimes balked at stripping them. Right Department Bureau official Wang Gang objected: "You hold the scales of state—where is the fairness in this?"

sentences.zh: 頤浩再秉政凡二年，高宗以水旱、地震，下詔罪己求言，頤浩連章待罪。

translations.literal: Yihao held power a second time for two years in all; Emperor Gaozong, on account of flood, drought, and earthquake, issued an edict blaming himself and seeking remonstrance; Yihao submitted successive memorials awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In his second stint in power, spanning two years, floods, drought, and earthquakes moved the emperor to issue a self-reproach edict inviting criticism; Yihao submitted one memorial after another offering to accept blame.

sentences.zh: 高宗一日謂大臣曰：「國朝四方水旱，無不上聞。

translations.literal: One day Emperor Gaozong said to the great ministers: "In our dynasty, flood and drought in the four directions have none that fail to be reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: One day Emperor Gaozong told his ministers, "In this dynasty no flood or drought anywhere in the realm has ever gone unreported.

sentences.zh: 近蘇、湖地震，泉州大水，輒不以奏，何也？」

translations.literal: Recently earthquakes in Su and Hu, great flood in Quanzhou—why were these not memorialized?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the earthquakes in Suzhou and Huzhou and the great flood at Quanzhou were never reported—why?

sentences.zh: 侍御史辛炳、殿中常同論其罪，遂罷頤浩為鎮南軍節度使、開府儀同三司、提舉洞霄宮，改特進、觀文殿大學士。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Xin Bing and Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Chang Tong together discussed his crimes; Yihao was thereupon removed and appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, Grand Master of the Palace with Imperial Order equal to the Three Excellencies, and Superintendent of the Tongxiao Palace, changed to Special Advancement and Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Xin Bing and Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Chang Tong joined in charging him; Lu Yihao was dismissed from the chief ministry and made Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, Grand Master of the Palace with rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and Superintendent of the Tongxiao Palace, with his title changed to Special Advancement and Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔問宰執以戰守方略，頤浩條十事以獻，除湖南安撫、制置大使兼知潭州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict asked the chief councillors for strategy in war and defense; Yihao listed ten items and presented them; he was appointed Hunan Pacification Commissioner and Military Affairs Commissioner concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor asked his chief councillors for plans of war and defense; Lu Yihao submitted a ten-point program and was appointed Hunan Pacification and Military Affairs Commissioner, concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時郴、衡、桂陽盜起，頤浩遣人悉平之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose in Chen, Heng, and Guiyang; Yihao sent men and fully pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits broke out in Chen, Heng, and Guiyang, he dispatched forces and put down every outbreak.

sentences.zh: 帝在建康，除頤浩少保、浙西安撫制置大使、知臨安府、行宮留守。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Jiankang; Yihao was appointed Junior Mentor, Zhexi Pacification and Military Affairs Commissioner, Prefect of Lin'an, and Keeper of the Mobile Palace.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor at Jiankang, Lu Yihao was made Junior Mentor, Zhexi Pacification and Military Affairs Commissioner, Prefect of Lin'an, and Keeper of the Mobile Palace.

sentences.zh: 明堂禮成，進封成國公。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall rites were completed, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bright Hall ceremony was completed, he was promoted in rank to Duke of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 八年，上將還臨安，除少傅、鎮南定江軍節度使、江東安撫制置大使兼知建康府、行宮留守。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, as the emperor was about to return to Lin'an, he was appointed Junior Tutor, Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Dingjiang Army, Jiangdong Pacification and Military Affairs Commissioner concurrently Prefect of Jiankang, and Keeper of the Mobile Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, as the court prepared to return to Lin'an, he was appointed Junior Tutor, Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Dingjiang Army, Jiangdong Pacification and Military Affairs Commissioner, concurrently Prefect of Jiankang and Keeper of the Mobile Palace.

sentences.zh: 頤浩引疾求去，除醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: Yihao cited illness and sought to leave office; he was appointed Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yihao pleaded illness and asked to resign; he was given the post of Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 九年，金人歸河南地，高宗欲以頤浩往陝西，命中使召赴行在。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Jurchens returned Henan territory; Gaozong wished to send Yihao to Shaanxi and ordered an imperial envoy to summon him to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, after the Jurchens returned Henan, Emperor Gaozong wanted to send Lu Yihao to Shaanxi and dispatched an imperial envoy to summon him to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 頤浩以老病辭，且條陝西利害，謂金人無故歸地，其必有意。

translations.literal: Yihao declined on grounds of age and illness, and also set forth the advantages and disadvantages of Shaanxi, saying the Jurchens had returned the land without cause and must have some design.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yihao declined on account of age and illness and laid out the strategic stakes in Shaanxi, arguing that the Jurchens would not surrender territory without ulterior motive.

sentences.zh: 召趣赴闕，既至，以疾不能見，乃聽歸。

translations.literal: He was summoned urgently to court; when he arrived, he was too ill to be received and was permitted to return.
translations.idiomatic: Urgently summoned to court, he arrived too ill to be received in audience and was allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，贈太師，封秦國公，諡忠穆。

translations.literal: Before long he died; posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed Duke of Qin, posthumous name Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qin, with the posthumous name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 頤浩有膽略，善鞍馬弓劍，當國步艱難之際，人倚之為重。

translations.literal: Yihao had courage and strategy, was skilled at saddle, horse, bow, and sword; at a time when the state's fortunes were perilous, people relied on him as a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yihao had boldness and strategic sense and was adept with horse, saddle, bow, and blade; in an age of national crisis, men looked to him as a mainstay.

sentences.zh: 自江東再相，胡安國以書勸其法韓忠獻，以至公無我為先，報復恩仇為戒，頤浩不能用。

translations.literal: From his second appointment as chief councillor in Jiangdong, Hu Anguo wrote urging him to follow the example of Han the Loyal and Beneficent, putting supreme impartiality and selflessness first and taking revenge for favors and grudges as a warning; Yihao could not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: After he became chief councillor again in the east, Hu Anguo wrote urging him to take Han Qi as his model—putting public duty above private feeling and shunning score-settling—and Lu Yihao would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 時軍用不足，頤浩與朱勝非創立江、浙、湖南諸路大軍月樁錢，於是郡邑多橫賦，大為東南患云。

translations.literal: When military funds were insufficient, Yihao and Zhu Shengfei created the monthly apportionment levy for major armies on the Jiang, Zhe, and Hunan circuits; thereafter prefectures and counties imposed many harsh exactions, greatly afflicting the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: When army funds ran short, Lu Yihao and Zhu Shengfei instituted monthly apportionment levies for the main forces in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Hunan; counties and prefectures then piled on harsh taxes, and the southeast suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 范宗尹

translations.literal: Fan Zongyin
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin

sentences.zh: 范宗尹，字覺民，襄陽鄧城人。

translations.literal: Fan Zongyin, style name Juemin, a man of Dengcheng in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin, styled Juemin, was a native of Dengcheng in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，工文辭。

translations.literal: From youth he studied devotedly and was adept at literary composition.
