translations.idiomatic: As a youth he applied himself to learning and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，上舍登第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe, he passed the upper hostel examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 3 he passed the upper hostel examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍御史、右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Supervising Censor and Right Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Supervising Censor and Right Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 王雲使北還，言金人必欲得三鎮。

translations.literal: Wang Yun returned from a mission north and said the Jurchens would surely demand the Three Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yun returned from his mission to the north, he reported that the Jurchens would certainly insist on taking the Three Prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宗尹請棄之以紓禍，言者非之，宗尹罷歸。

translations.literal: Zongyin requested abandoning them to avert disaster; critics denounced this and Zongyin was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin urged surrendering the prefectures to ward off catastrophe; critics attacked the proposal, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭位，復其職，遣同路允迪詣康王勸進。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne, Zongyin's office was restored; he was sent with Lu Yundi to urge the Prince of Kang to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Bangchang seized the throne, Fan Zongyin was restored to office and sent with Lu Yundi to persuade the Prince of Kang to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，李綱拜右僕射，宗尹論其名浮於實，有震主之威。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan, Li Gang was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Zongyin argued his reputation exceeded his substance and that he had a bearing that overawed the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1, when Li Gang was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Fan Zongyin charged that his fame outran his ability and that he carried himself in a way that intimidated the throne.

sentences.zh: 不報，出知舒州。

translations.literal: There was no response; he was sent out as Prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not reply, and he was sent out to serve as Prefect of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者論宗尹嘗汙偽命，責置鄂州。

translations.literal: Critics argued Zongyin had once been tainted by a false edict and he was demoted and assigned to Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that Fan Zongyin had once been compromised by a usurper's commission, and he was demoted and posted to Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 既，召為中書舍人，遷御史中丞，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was recalled as Drafting Official of the Secretariat, promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled as Secretariat Drafting Official, promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, and appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩罷相，宗尹攝其位。

translations.literal: When Lu Yihao was removed as chief councillor, Zongyin acted in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yihao left the chief ministry, Fan Zongyin stepped in to fill the vacancy.

sentences.zh: 時諸盜據有州縣，朝廷力不能制。

translations.literal: At the time various bandits held prefectures and counties and the court lacked the strength to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits then held prefectures and counties across the land, and the court lacked the power to dislodge them.

sentences.zh: 宗尹言：「太祖收藩鎮之權，天下無事百五十年，可謂良法。

translations.literal: Zongyin said: "Taizu recovered the powers of the military commissioners; the realm was at peace for a hundred and fifty years—a praiseworthy method.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin said, "When Taizu stripped the military commissioners of their powers, the empire enjoyed a century and a half of peace—that was sound policy.

sentences.zh: 然國家多難，四方帥守單寡，束手環視，此法之弊。

translations.literal: Yet in the state's many calamities, commanders and prefects in the four directions are few and isolated, standing by with folded hands and looking on—this is the flaw of the method.
translations.idiomatic: But in our present troubles, frontier commanders and prefects are too few and too weak; they can only stand by helplessly—that is where the policy fails.

sentences.zh: 今當稍復藩鎮之法，裂河南、江北數十州之地，付以兵權，俾蕃王室。

translations.literal: Now we should slightly restore the method of military commissioners, dividing dozens of prefectures south of the river and north of the Huai and entrusting them with military authority to shield the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: We should now partly revive the military-commissioner system, carving out several dozen prefectures south of the Yellow River and north of the Huai, granting them military authority to defend the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 較之棄地夷狄，豈不相遠？」

translations.literal: Compared with abandoning territory to the barbarians, is this not far better?
translations.idiomatic: Surely that is far preferable to simply yielding the land to foreign invaders?"

sentences.zh: 上從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 授宗尹通議大夫、守尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼禦營使，時年三十。

translations.literal: Zongyin was appointed Grand Master for Proper Counsel, acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-ordinator of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Commissioner of the Imperial Camp; he was then thirty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin was appointed Grand Master for Proper Counsel, acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-ordinator of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Commissioner of the Imperial Camp—at the age of thirty.

sentences.zh: 近世宰相年少，未有如宗尹者。

translations.literal: In recent times no chief councillor so young as Zongyin had been seen.
translations.idiomatic: No chief councillor in recent memory had been as young as Fan Zongyin.

sentences.zh: 宗尹奏以京畿東西、淮南、湖北地並分為鎮，授諸將，以鎮撫使為名；

translations.literal: Zongyin memorialized that the eastern and western capital districts, Huainan, and Hubei should all be divided into jurisdictions and conferred on various generals under the title of Pacification Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin proposed dividing the eastern and western capital regions, Huainan, and Hubei into separate jurisdictions and appointing generals to them as Pacification Commissioners;

sentences.zh: 軍興，聽便宜從事。

translations.literal: in time of military emergency, they were permitted to act on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: during wartime they would be allowed to act at their own discretion.

sentences.zh: 然李成、薛慶、孔彥舟、桑仲輩起於群盜，翟興、劉位土豪，李彥光、郭仲威皆潰將，多不能守其地。

translations.literal: Yet Li Cheng, Xue Qing, Kong Yanchuan, Sang Zhong, and the like had risen from among bandit hordes; Zhai Xing and Liu Wei were local magnates; Li Yanguang and Guo Zhongwei were all routed generals—most could not hold their territories.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Cheng, Xue Qing, Kong Yanchuan, Sang Zhong, and others were former bandit chiefs; Zhai Xing and Liu Wei were local strongmen; Li Yanguang and Guo Zhongwei were broken generals—and most proved unable to keep their assigned territories.

sentences.zh: 宗尹請有司討論崇、觀以來濫賞，修書、營繕、應奉、開河、免夫、獄空之類，皆厘正之。

translations.literal: Zongyin requested that the relevant offices review lavish rewards since the Chongning and Xuanhe reigns—compilation of books, construction and repair, tribute service, river digging, exemption of corvée, empty prisons, and the like—and rectify them all.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin asked the appropriate offices to review excessive rewards granted since the Chongning and Xuanhe reigns—book projects, construction, tribute missions, canal work, corvée exemptions, claims of empty prisons, and the like—and set them right.

sentences.zh: 宣靖執政、圍城、明受偽命之人，反用赦申雪；

translations.literal: Those who held power during the Xuanhe and Jingkang years, besieged the capital, or openly accepted false edicts were instead cleared through amnesties;
translations.idiomatic: Men who had governed during the Xuanhe and Jingkang crises, who had been involved in the siege of the capital, or who had openly accepted forged commissions were instead rehabilitated through amnesties;

sentences.zh: 徐秉哲、吳幵、莫儔等並量移；

translations.literal: Xu Bingzhe, Wu Kai, Mo Chou, and others were all transferred by reduced appointment;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bingzhe, Wu Kai, Mo Chou, and others were merely transferred to lesser posts;

sentences.zh: 吳敏、王孝迪、耿南仲、孫覿、蔡懋等並敘復。

translations.literal: Wu Min, Wang Xiaodi, Geng Nanzhong, Sun Di, Cai Mao, and others were all restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: while Wu Min, Wang Xiaodi, Geng Nanzhong, Sun Di, Cai Mao, and others were fully restored to rank.

sentences.zh: 侍郎季陵希宗尹意，乞詔宰執於罪累中選真材實能，量付以事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Ji Ling, courting Zongyin's intent, requested an edict that chief councillors select men of genuine talent and real ability from among those with tainted records and assign them duties as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Ji Ling, seeking to please Fan Zongyin, asked that the chief councillors be ordered to pick men of real talent from among those with blemished records and employ them according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 沈與求劾陵，因及宗尹，宗尹求去。

translations.literal: Shen Yuqiu impeached Ji Ling and thereby implicated Zongyin; Zongyin sought to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yuqiu impeached Ji Ling and by extension attacked Fan Zongyin, who then asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 上為罷與求，宗尹乃復視事。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Shen Yuqiu on his account, and Zongyin resumed duties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor removed Shen Yuqiu to placate him, and Fan Zongyin returned to office.

sentences.zh: 初，宗尹廷對，詳定官李邦彥特取旨置宗尹乙科，宗尹德之，贈邦彥觀文殿大學士。

translations.literal: Initially, at Zongyin's court audience, Assessing Official Li Bangyan had specially obtained imperial instruction to place Zongyin in the second examination rank; Zongyin was grateful and posthumously awarded Bangyan Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at Fan Zongyin's palace examination, Assessing Official Li Bangyan had obtained a special imperial order placing him in the second rank; grateful, Fan Zongyin later posthumously granted Bangyan the title Grand Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture.

sentences.zh: 樞密院副都承旨闕，宗尹擬刑煥、藍公佐、辛道宗三人，煥戚里，公佐管客省，道宗不知兵，人以此咎宗尹。

translations.literal: The post of Deputy Chief Palace Liaison of the Bureau of Military Affairs was vacant; Zongyin proposed three men—Xing Huan, Lan Gongzuo, and Xin Daozong; Huan was a consort kinsman, Gongzuo managed the Reception Office, and Daozong knew nothing of military affairs; people blamed Zongyin for this.
translations.idiomatic: When the deputy chief palace liaison post at the Bureau of Military Affairs fell vacant, Fan Zongyin nominated Xing Huan, Lan Gongzuo, and Xin Daozong—Huan was an imperial in-law, Gongzuo ran the guest reception office, and Daozong was ignorant of military affairs—and critics held Fan Zongyin responsible.

sentences.zh: 密院計議官王佾結公佐，宗尹請除佾為宗正丞，侍御史張延壽劾之，上罷佾。

translations.literal: Planning Official Wang Yi of the Bureau of Military Affairs bonded with Gongzuo; Zongyin requested appointing Yi as Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Clans; Supervising Censor Zhang Yanshou impeached him and the emperor dismissed Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, a planning officer at the Bureau of Military Affairs, cultivated ties with Lan Gongzuo; Fan Zongyin sought to appoint Wang Yi Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Clans, but Supervising Censor Zhang Yanshou impeached him and the emperor removed Wang Yi from office.

sentences.zh: 宗尹有才智，當北敵肆行之沖，毅然自任，建議分鎮，以是得相位。

translations.literal: Zongyin had talent and intelligence; when the northern enemy ran rampant at the frontier, he resolutely took responsibility, proposed dividing jurisdictions, and thereby gained the chief councillorship.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin was clever and capable; as the northern foe pressed hard on the frontier, he boldly shouldered responsibility, proposed the division of military jurisdictions, and thereby won the chief ministry.

sentences.zh: 然其置帥多授劇盜，又無總率統屬，且不遣援，不通餉，故諸鎮守鮮能久存者。

translations.literal: Yet in appointing commanders he mostly invested fierce bandits; there was also no overall command hierarchy, no relief forces were sent, and supplies were not forwarded—so few jurisdiction defenders could long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he mostly installed notorious bandit leaders as commanders, provided no unified chain of command, sent no reinforcements, and forwarded no supplies—so few of his regional defenders lasted long.

sentences.zh: 及為政多私，屢為議者所詆云。

translations.literal: Moreover his governance was largely self-serving, and he was repeatedly denounced by critics.
translations.idiomatic: He also governed with heavy favoritism and was repeatedly attacked by critics.

sentences.zh: 範致虛

translations.literal: Fan Zhixu
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu

sentences.zh: 範致虛，字謙叔，建州建陽人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhixu, style name Qianshu, a man of Jianyang in Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu, styled Qianshu, was a native of Jianyang in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為太學博士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and became an Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 鄒浩以言事斥，致虛坐祖送獲罪，停官。

translations.literal: When Zou Hao was expelled for remonstrance, Zhixu was punished for escorting him on his way and was suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zou Hao was banished for speaking out, Fan Zhixu was punished for seeing him off on his journey and was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 徽宗嗣位，召見，除左正言，出通判郢州。

translations.literal: When Huizong succeeded to the throne, he was summoned for an audience, appointed Left Rectifier, and sent out as Vice Prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Huizong ascended the throne, he was summoned to audience, appointed Left Rectifier, and dispatched as Vice Prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，以右司諫召，道改起居舍人，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, he was recalled as Right Remonstrance Official of the Department of State Affairs; en route his appointment was changed to Recorder of the Palace, and he was advanced to Drafting Official of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongning era he was recalled as Right Remonstrance Official of the Department of State Affairs; before he arrived his appointment was changed to Palace Recorder, and he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Official.

sentences.zh: 蔡京建請置講議司，引致虛為詳定官，議不合，改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Cai Jing memorialized to establish the Deliberation Office and brought in Zhixu as Assessing Official; when their views did not agree, he was changed to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing proposed creating the Deliberation Office and brought Fan Zhixu in as an assessing official; when they disagreed, Fan Zhixu was transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 自是入處華要，出典大郡者十五年。

translations.literal: From then on he alternated between holding lofty central posts and governing great prefectures for fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: For the next fifteen years he moved between high central offices and major prefectural commands.

sentences.zh: 以附張商英，貶通州。

translations.literal: For associating with Zhang Shangying, he was demoted to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his ties to Zhang Shangying, he was demoted and sent to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 政和七年，復官，入為侍讀、修國史，尋除刑部尚書、提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenghe, his office was restored; he entered service as Lecturer-in-Waiting and Compiler of the National History, and soon was appointed Minister of Justice and Superintendent of the Hongqing Palace at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 7 his rank was restored; he entered court as Lecturer-in-Waiting and Compiler of the National History, and soon became Minister of Justice and Superintendent of the Hongqing Palace at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 初，致虛在講議司，延康殿學士劉昺嘗乘蔡京怒擠之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhixu was in the Deliberation Office, Hanlin Academician Liu Bing had once taken advantage of Cai Jing's anger to squeeze him out.
translations.idiomatic: While Fan Zhixu served in the Deliberation Office, Hanlin Academician Liu Bing had once exploited Cai Jing's displeasure to force him out.

sentences.zh: 後王寀坐妖言系獄，事連昺論死，致虛爭之，昺得減竄，士論賢之。

translations.literal: Later Wang Cai was imprisoned on charges of sorcery and heterodox speech; the case implicated Bing, who was sentenced to death; Zhixu argued on his behalf and Bing's punishment was reduced to exile; learned opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Cai was jailed on charges of sorcery and seditious talk; the case dragged in Liu Bing, who was sentenced to death; Fan Zhixu intervened, Liu Bing's sentence was reduced to exile, and scholars praised Fan Zhixu for it.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞，進左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and advanced to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and then to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 母喪逾年，起知東平府，改大名府。

translations.literal: After more than a year of mourning for his mother, he was recalled to serve as Prefect of Dongping and then transferred to Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning after more than a year, he was made Prefect of Dongping and then transferred to Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入見，時朝廷欲用師契丹，致虛言邊隙一開，必有意外之患。

translations.literal: On entering audience, the court then wished to use troops against the Khitans; Zhixu said that once the frontier was opened to conflict, unforeseen calamities would surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: When he appeared at court, the government was preparing to campaign against the Khitans; Fan Zhixu warned that once hostilities began at the frontier, unexpected disasters would follow.

sentences.zh: 宰相謂其懷異。

translations.literal: The chief councillors said he harbored dissenting views.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillors accused him of disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 致虛乞終喪，從之。

translations.literal: Zhixu requested to complete his mourning period and was granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu asked to finish his mourning leave and was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 免喪，知鄧州，改河南府。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was Prefect of Dengzhou, then transferred to Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as Prefect of Dengzhou and was then transferred to Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中人規景華苑，欲奪故相富弼園宅。

translations.literal: A eunuch planned the Jinghua Garden and wished to seize the garden residence of the former chief councillor Fu Bi.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch laid plans for the Jinghua Garden and sought to confiscate the garden estate of the former chief councillor Fu Bi.

sentences.zh: 致虛言：「弼和戎有大功，使朝廷享百年之安，乃不保數畝之居邪？」

translations.literal: Zhixu said: "Bi's achievement in making peace with the Rong had great merit and enabled the court to enjoy a century of security—shall he not be allowed to keep a few mu of dwelling?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu said, "Fu Bi's peace with the Khitans brought the court a century of security—are we now to deny him even a few acres of home?"

sentences.zh: 弼園宅得不取。

translations.literal: Fu Bi's garden residence was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi's garden estate was spared.

sentences.zh: 復移鄧州、提舉亳州明道宮。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Dengzhou and appointed Superintendent of the Mingdao Palace at Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to Dengzhou and made Superintendent of the Mingdao Palace at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 帝方好老氏，致虛希時好，營飭道宇，賜名煉真宮。

translations.literal: The emperor was then fond of Laozi; Zhixu catered to the prevailing taste, built and adorned a Daoist temple, which was granted the name Lianzhen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then devoted to Daoism; Fan Zhixu played to the fashion, built and refurbished a Daoist temple, and received the imperial name Lianzhen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，召赴闕，道除知京兆府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, he was summoned to court; en route he was appointed Prefect of Jingzhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1 he was summoned to the capital and, while still en route, was appointed Prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時金人圍太原，聲震關中，致虛修戰守備甚力。

translations.literal: At the time the Jurchens besieged Taiyuan and the alarm shook the Guanzhong region; Zhixu exerted himself greatly in preparing defenses for war and siege.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jurchens besieged Taiyuan and panic spread through Guanzhong, Fan Zhixu worked tirelessly to prepare the region for war and siege.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命錢蓋節制陝西，除致虛陝西宣撫使。

translations.literal: The court appointed Qian Gai to command Shaanxi and made Zhixu Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The court put Qian Gai in overall command of Shaanxi and appointed Fan Zhixu Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 金人分道再犯京師，詔致虛會兵入援。

translations.literal: The Jurchens invaded the capital again by separate routes; an edict ordered Zhixu to gather troops and march to the relief of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens struck the capital again on multiple fronts, an edict ordered Fan Zhixu to assemble troops and march to its relief.

sentences.zh: 錢蓋兵十萬至潁昌，聞京師破而遁，西道總管王襄南走。

translations.literal: Qian Gai's army of a hundred thousand reached Yingchang, heard the capital had fallen, and fled; Western Route Commander-in-Chief Wang Xiang fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gai's force of one hundred thousand reached Yingchang, learned that the capital had fallen, and fled; Western Route Commander Wang Xiang also broke south.

sentences.zh: 致虛獨與西道副總管孫昭遠合兵，環慶帥臣王似、熙河帥臣王倚以兵來會。

translations.literal: Zhixu alone joined forces with Western Route Deputy Commander-in-Chief Sun Zhaoyuan; the military commissioners of Huanqing and Xihe, Wang Si and Wang Yi, came with troops to rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu alone combined with Western Route Deputy Commander Sun Zhaoyuan, while the commissioners of Huanqing and Xihe, Wang Si and Wang Yi, marched to join him.

sentences.zh: 致虛合步騎號二十萬，以右武大夫馬昌祐統之，命杜常將民兵萬人趨京師，夏俶將萬人守陵寢。

translations.literal: Zhixu assembled infantry and cavalry reckoned at two hundred thousand, put them under Right Martial Grand Master Ma Changyou, ordered Du Chang to lead ten thousand militia toward the capital, and Xia Shu to lead ten thousand to guard the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu mustered infantry and cavalry said to number two hundred thousand under Right Martial Grand Master Ma Changyou, sent Du Chang with ten thousand militia toward the capital, and Xia Shu with ten thousand to guard the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 兵有僧趙宗印者，喜談兵，席益薦之。

translations.literal: Among the troops was the monk Zhao Zongyin, who loved to discourse on military matters; Xi Yi recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: In the army was a monk named Zhao Zongyin who loved to talk of war; Xi Yi recommended him.

sentences.zh: 致虛以便宜假官，俾充宣撫司參議官兼節制軍馬。

translations.literal: Zhixu provisionally granted him an office by special authority and had him serve as Planning Official of the Pacification Commission concurrently commanding army and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu granted him a provisional appointment by special authority and made him planning officer of the pacification commission with concurrent command of the forces.

sentences.zh: 致虛以大軍遵陸，宗印以舟師趨西京。

translations.literal: Zhixu moved the main army overland while Zongyin led the river fleet toward the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu marched the main force by land while Zhao Zongyin took the river fleet toward the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 金人破京師，遣人持登城不下之詔，以止入援之師，致虛斬之。

translations.literal: The Jurchens took the capital and sent men bearing an edict demanding that the city not be held, intending to stop the relief armies; Zhixu had them executed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens captured the capital they sent envoys with an edict ordering the city not to resist, hoping to halt the relief columns; Fan Zhixu had the bearers executed.

sentences.zh: 初，金人守潼關，致虛奪之，作長城，起潼關迄龍門，所築僅及肩。

translations.literal: Initially the Jurchens held Tong Pass; Zhixu seized it and built a long wall from Tong Pass to Longmen, but what was constructed reached only to shoulder height.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens had held Tong Pass; Fan Zhixu recaptured it and built a long rampart from Tong Pass to Longmen, though the work rose only to shoulder height.

sentences.zh: 宗印又以僧為一軍，號「尊勝隊」，童子行為一軍，號「淨勝隊」。

translations.literal: Zongyin also formed one army of monks called the "Honored Victory Corps" and one of boy acolytes called the "Pure Victory Corps."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zongyin also organized a monk corps called the Honored Victory Detachment and a corps of boy acolytes called the Pure Victory Detachment.

sentences.zh: 致虛勇而無謀，委己以聽宗印。

translations.literal: Zhixu was brave but lacked strategy and entrusted himself entirely to Zongyin's judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu was bold but not shrewd and left all decisions to Zhao Zongyin.

sentences.zh: 宗印徒大言，實未嘗知兵。

translations.literal: Zongyin was merely grand in talk and in truth had never known military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zongyin talked big but in fact knew nothing of war.

sentences.zh: 至是，宗印舟師至三門津，致虛使整兵出潼關。

translations.literal: At this point Zongyin's fleet reached Sanmen Ford; Zhixu ordered the army marshaled and marched out through Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zongyin's fleet reached Sanmen Ford, Fan Zhixu drew up his troops and marched out through Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 金守臣高世由謂其帥粘罕曰：「致虛儒者，不知兵，遣斥候三千，自足殺之。」

translations.literal: Jin defender Gao Shiyou said to his commander Nianhan: "Zhixu is a Confucian who knows nothing of war; send three thousand scouts—that alone will be enough to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin officer Gao Shiyou told his commander Nianhan, "Fan Zhixu is a bookish man who knows nothing of war—three thousand scouts will be enough to finish him off.

sentences.zh: 致虛軍出武關，至鄧州千秋鎮，金將婁宿以精騎沖之，不戰而潰，死者過半。

translations.literal: Zhixu's army marched out through Wu Pass to Qianqiu Post in Dengzhou; the Jurchen general Wusu charged with elite cavalry; without fighting they scattered; more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu's army marched out through Wu Pass to Qianqiu Post in Dengzhou, where the Jurchen general Wusu struck with elite cavalry; the Song force broke without a fight and more than half were killed.

sentences.zh: 杜常、夏俶先遁，致虛斬之。

translations.literal: Du Chang and Xia Shu fled first; Zhixu had them executed.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chang and Xia Shu had fled first; Fan Zhixu had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 孫昭遠、王似、王倚等留陝府，致虛收餘兵入潼關。

translations.literal: Sun Zhaoyuan, Wang Si, Wang Yi, and others remained at Shaanxi Prefecture; Zhixu gathered the remnant troops and withdrew into Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhaoyuan, Wang Si, Wang Yi, and the others stayed at Shaanxi Prefecture while Fan Zhixu collected the survivors and pulled back into Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 方致虛之鼓行出關也，裨將李彥仙曰：「行者利速，多為支軍，則舍不至淹，敗不至覆。

translations.literal: Just as Zhixu was beating drums and marching out of the pass, staff general Li Yanxian said: "Marchers benefit from speed; make many detached columns, then baggage camps will not be delayed and defeat will not become total disaster.
translations.idiomatic: As Fan Zhixu was beating drums and marching out of the pass, staff general Li Yanxian warned, "An army on the move needs speed; send out many detachments so supply camps are not held up and a setback does not become a rout.

sentences.zh: 若眾群聚而出殽、澠，一蹴於險，則皆潰矣。」

translations.literal: If the host masses together through Yao and Mian and is struck once in narrow terrain, all will flee."
translations.idiomatic: If the whole force crowds through Yao and Mian and is hit once in the defiles, everyone will scatter."

sentences.zh: 致虛不聽，遂底於敗。

translations.literal: Zhixu would not listen and thereby came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu refused to listen and marched straight to disaster.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，言者論其逗撓不進，徙知鄧州。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, critics charged him with delay and reluctance to advance; he was transferred to serve as Prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong took the throne, critics accused Fan Zhixu of dawdling and failing to advance, and he was transferred to Prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋加觀文殿學士，復知京兆府；

translations.literal: Soon he was given the title Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture and again appointed Prefect of Jingzhao;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Academician of the Hall for Veneration of Culture and again appointed Prefect of Jingzhao;

sentences.zh: 致虛力辭，而薦席益、李彌大、唐重自代。

translations.literal: Zhixu forcefully declined and recommended Xi Yi, Li Mida, and Tang Zhong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu firmly declined the post and recommended Xi Yi, Li Mida, and Tang Zhong to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以重守京兆，致虛復知鄧州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhong to defend Jingzhao; Zhixu was again made Prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By edict Tang Zhong was put in charge of Jingzhao, and Fan Zhixu was again appointed Prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 次年，宗印領兵出武關，與致虛合。

translations.literal: The next year, Zongyin led troops out through Wu Pass and joined with Zhixu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhao Zongyin led his troops out through Wu Pass and united with Fan Zhixu.

sentences.zh: 會金將銀朱兵壓境，致虛遁，宗印兵不戰走，轉運使劉汲力戰死焉。

translations.literal: When the Jin general Yinzhu pressed the border with his army, Zhixu fled; Zongyin's troops retreated without fighting; Transport Commissioner Liu Ji fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen general Yinzhu brought his army to the frontier, Fan Zhixu fled, Zhao Zongyin's force withdrew without a fight, and Transport Commissioner Liu Ji died fighting.

sentences.zh: 致虛坐落職，責授安遠軍節度副使，英州安置。

translations.literal: Zhixu was stripped of his post, demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Anyuan Army, and assigned to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu was dismissed from office, reduced to Vice Military Commissioner of the Anyuan Army, and posted to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸建康，召復資政殿學士、知鼎州。

translations.literal: When Gaozong traveled to Jiankang, he was recalled as Academician of the Hall for Administration of State Affairs and Prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong went to Jiankang, Fan Zhixu was recalled as Academician of the Hall for Administration of State Affairs and appointed Prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至巴陵卒，贈銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died at Baling while on the road and was posthumously awarded Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Baling en route and was posthumously granted the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 呂好問

translations.literal: Lu Haowen
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen

sentences.zh: 呂好問，字舜徒，侍講希哲子也。

translations.literal: Lu Haowen, style name Shuntu, was the son of Director of Lectures Xizhe.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen, styled Shuntu, was the son of the Director of Lectures, Lu Xizhe.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補官。

translations.literal: He entered office through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He received his first appointment through inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 崇甯初，治黨事，好問以元祐子弟坐廢。

translations.literal: Early in Chongning, during the party purge, Haowen was dismissed as a member of the Yuanyou faction.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongning era, when factional cases were prosecuted, Lu Haowen was removed from office as a Yuanyou partisan.

sentences.zh: 兩監東嶽廟，司揚州儀曹。

translations.literal: Twice he served as Superintendent of the Eastern Peak Temple and held the post of Master of Protocol in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He twice superintended the Eastern Peak Temple and served as Master of Protocol in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蔡卞為帥，欲扳附善類，待好問特異。

translations.literal: When Cai Bian was regional commander, he wished to win over men of virtue and treated Haowen with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: While Cai Bian was military commissioner, he sought to attach good men to himself and treated Lu Haowen with unusual regard.

sentences.zh: 好問以禮自持，卞不得親。

translations.literal: Haowen maintained himself by ritual propriety, and Bian could not draw close.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen held himself aloof with proper decorum, and Bian could not win his intimacy.

sentences.zh: 及卞得政，當時據屬拔擢略盡，獨好問留滯，卞諷之曰：「子少親我，即階顯列矣。」

translations.literal: When Bian came to power, nearly all his followers had been promoted; Haowen alone remained stuck in low office. Bian hinted: "If you had only drawn close to me, you would already have risen to high rank."
translations.idiomatic: Once Bian took power, he had promoted nearly every man in his circle; only Lu Haowen still languished in a minor post. Bian insinuated, "Had you only befriended me, you would long since have reached the highest ranks."

sentences.zh: 好問笑不答。

translations.literal: Haowen smiled and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，以薦召為左司諫、諫議大夫，擢御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, on recommendation he was summoned as Left Remonstrance Official and Remonstrance Grandee, then promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1, on recommendation he was called up as Left Remonstrance Official and Remonstrance Grandee, then elevated to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 欽宗諭之曰：「卿元祐子孫，朕特用卿，令天下知朕意所向。」

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong instructed him: "You are of Yuanyou descent; I am using you specially so all under Heaven will know where my intentions lie."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong told him, "You come from a Yuanyou family; I am appointing you deliberately so the empire will know where my mind is set."

sentences.zh: 先是，徽宗將內禪，詔解黨禁，除新法，盡復祖宗之故。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huizong was about to abdicate in favor of his successor, an edict lifted the factional ban, abolished the New Policies, and fully restored the ancestral ways.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, as Huizong prepared to abdicate, he had issued an edict lifting the factional proscriptions, repealing the New Policies, and restoring the institutions of former emperors.

sentences.zh: 而蔡京黨戚根據中外，害其事，莫肯行。

translations.literal: But Cai Jing's partisans and kinsmen had entrenched themselves throughout court and country, obstructed the plan, and refused to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cai Jing's faction and relatives had rooted themselves inside and outside the court, sabotaged the effort, and would not execute it.

sentences.zh: 好問言：「時之利害，政之闕失，太上皇?旨備矣。

translations.literal: Haowen said: "The advantages and harms of the times and the failings of government—the Retired Emperor's edicts have already laid them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen said, "The pressing gains and losses of the age and the defects of policy—the Retired Emperor's edicts have already covered them completely.

sentences.zh: 雖使直言之士抗疏論列，無以過此，願一一施行之而已。」

translations.literal: Even if blunt-speaking men were to submit memorials enumerating faults, they could not surpass this; I only ask that each measure be carried out one by one."
translations.idiomatic: Even the frankest remonstrators could add nothing beyond what those edicts already say; I ask only that they be put into effect, one by one."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下宵衣旰食，有求治之意；

translations.literal: He added: "Your Majesty rises before dawn and eats after dusk—you have the will to seek good governance;
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "Your Majesty rises at dawn and eats late into the evening—you clearly mean to bring order to the realm;

sentences.zh: 發號施令，有求治之言。

translations.literal: you issue orders and decrees with language that seeks good governance.
translations.idiomatic: your proclamations and commands all speak of the same desire for good government.

sentences.zh: 逮今半載，治效逾邈，良田左右前後，不能推廣德意，而陛下過於容養。

translations.literal: Yet half a year has passed and the effects of governance grow ever more distant; the good ministers at your side fail to spread your virtuous intent, while Your Majesty is too indulgent in tolerating them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet six months have passed and results are farther off than ever; the worthy ministers around you have not carried your benevolent purpose into practice, while Your Majesty is too lenient toward them.

sentences.zh: 臣恐淳厚之德，變為頹靡，且今不盡革京、貫等所為，太平無由可致。」

translations.literal: I fear your genuine generosity will turn into lax indulgence; and unless the deeds of Jing, Guan, and their like are thoroughly reformed, there is no path to peace."
translations.idiomatic: I fear your native sincerity will decay into slackness; and unless everything done by Cai Jing, Tong Guan, and their kind is thoroughly undone, peace cannot be restored."

sentences.zh: 欽宗鄉納。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong approved it warmly."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong accepted the advice with approval."

sentences.zh: 好問疏蔡京過惡，乞役海外，黜朋附之尤者以厲其餘。

translations.literal: Haowen memorialized Cai Jing's crimes and wickedness, asking that he be sent to serve overseas, and that the worst of his partisans be dismissed to warn the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen submitted a memorial detailing Cai Jing's crimes and asked that he be exiled overseas and that the worst of his followers be removed to warn the others.

sentences.zh: 又建白削王安石王爵，正神宗配饗，褒表江公望，張庭堅、任伯雨、龔?等，除青苗之令，湔元符上書獲譴者，章前後疏十上。

translations.literal: He also proposed stripping Wang Anshi of his princely title, correcting Shenzong's sacrificial pairing, honoring Jiang Gongwang, Zhang Tingjian, Ren Boyu, Gong Mao, and others, abolishing the Green Sprouts order, and cleansing those punished for memorializing during Yuanfu—ten memorials in all, forward and back.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged stripping Wang Anshi of his princely rank, correcting the arrangement of Shenzong's spirit tablet in the ancestral temple, restoring honor to Jiang Gongwang, Zhang Tingjian, Ren Boyu, Gong Mao, and others, repealing the Green Sprouts law, and rehabilitating those punished for submitting memorials in the Yuanfu era—ten memorials in all, submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 每奏對，帝雖當食，輒使畢其說。

translations.literal: At each audience, even when the emperor was at mealtime, he always had Haowen finish speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Lu Haowen was received in audience, the emperor, even at mealtimes, always let him finish what he had to say.

sentences.zh: 時金人既退，大臣不復顧慮，武備益弛。

translations.literal: The Jurchens had already withdrawn, but the chief ministers no longer took thought for defense, and military readiness slackened further.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Jurchens had already pulled back, the chief ministers ceased to worry about defense, and military preparations grew laxer by the day.

sentences.zh: 好問言：「金人得志，益輕中國，秋冬必傾國復來，禦敵之備，當速講求。

translations.literal: Haowen said: "Having gotten their way, the Jurchens despise China all the more; in autumn and winter they will surely throw the whole realm into another invasion. Preparations to resist the enemy must be urgently discussed and sought.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen warned, "Emboldened by success, the Jurchens hold the Song in ever greater contempt; come autumn and winter they will surely return in full force. Defensive preparations must be debated and put in place at once.

sentences.zh: 今邊事經畫旬月，不見施設，臣僚奏請皆不行下，此臣所深懼也。」

translations.literal: For months now frontier affairs have been planned without any implementation; officials' memorials and requests are not issued downward—this is what I deeply fear."
translations.idiomatic: Border plans have been under discussion for months without a single measure being carried out; memorials from officials never receive approval—this is what terrifies me."

sentences.zh: 及邊警急，大臣不知所出，遣使講解。

translations.literal: When the frontier alarm grew urgent, the chief ministers knew not what to do and sent envoys to negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: When the border crisis sharpened, the chief ministers were at a loss and dispatched envoys to negotiate.

sentences.zh: 金人佯許而攻略自如，諸將以和議故，皆閉壁不出。

translations.literal: The Jurchens feigned agreement but attacked as they pleased; because of the peace talks, all the generals shut their walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens pretended to agree while pressing their attacks; trusting in the talks, the generals kept their gates closed and refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 好問言：「彼名和而實攻，朝廷不謀進兵遣將，何也？

translations.literal: Haowen said: "They talk peace while they actually attack—why does the court not plan to advance troops and dispatch generals?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen asked, "They call it peace while they make war—why does the court not mobilize armies and send out commanders?

sentences.zh: 請亟集滄、滑、邢、相之戍，以遏奔沖，而列勤王之師於畿邑，以衛京城。」

translations.literal: I ask that you immediately gather the garrisons of Cang, Hua, Xing, and Xiang to block rushing assaults, and array the armies that came to rescue the throne in the capital region to defend the imperial city."
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to concentrate the garrisons of Cang, Hua, Xing, and Xiang at once to check enemy thrusts, and to station the relief armies from the capital districts around the city to protect the throne."

sentences.zh: 疏上不省。

translations.literal: The memorial went up and received no attention.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted and ignored.

sentences.zh: 金人陷真定，攻中山，上下震駭，廷臣狐疑相顧，猶以和議為辭。

translations.literal: The Jurchens took Zhending and attacked Zhongshan; court and country were shaken; ministers looked at one another in doubt, still pleading for peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens captured Zhending and attacked Zhongshan, the court was terrified; ministers glanced at one another in uncertainty, still invoking peace negotiations.

sentences.zh: 好問率臺屬劾大臣畏懦誤國，出好問知袁州。

translations.literal: Haowen led his censorate staff in impeaching the chief ministers for cowardice and harming the state—and Haowen himself was sent out as Prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen led the censorate in impeaching the chief ministers for cowardice and betrayal of the state—and was himself transferred out as Prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 欽宗憫其忠，下遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong, pitying his loyalty, only demoted him to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong, moved by his loyalty, merely reduced him to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 既而金人薄都城，欽宗思好問言，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon the Jurchens pressed the capital; Emperor Qinzong recalled Haowen's words and promoted him to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens closed on the capital, Emperor Qinzong remembered Lu Haowen's warnings and promoted him to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 都城失守，召好問入禁中，軍民數萬斧左掖門求見天子，好問從帝御樓諭遣之。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Haowen was summoned into the forbidden precincts; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians axed through the Left Side Gate seeking an audience with the Son of Heaven; Haowen followed the emperor to the tower and ordered them dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was lost, Lu Haowen was called into the inner palace; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians hacked their way to the Left Side Gate demanding to see the emperor; Lu Haowen accompanied the emperor to the tower and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 衛士長蔣宣帥其徒數百，欲邀乘輿犯圍而出，左右奔竄，獨好問與孫傅、梅執禮侍，宣抗聲曰：「國事至此，皆宰相信任奸臣，不用直言所致。」

translations.literal: Captain of the guard Jiang Xuan led several hundred of his men, intending to intercept the imperial carriage and break through the encirclement; those around fled in panic; only Haowen, Sun Fu, and Mei Zhili remained in attendance. Jiang shouted: "Affairs have come to this because the chief councillors trusted wicked men and would not hear blunt counsel!"
translations.idiomatic: The guard captain Jiang Xuan rallied several hundred men, intending to seize the imperial carriage and break out of the siege; the attendants scattered in panic, leaving only Lu Haowen, Sun Fu, and Mei Zhili at the emperor's side. Jiang cried out, "The state has come to this because the chief councillors put their faith in wicked men and refused to heed honest counsel!"

sentences.zh: 傅呵之。

translations.literal: Fu scolded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 宣以語侵傅，好問曉之曰：「若屬忘家族，欲冒重圍衛上以出，誠忠義。

translations.literal: Jiang's words insulted Fu; Haowen reasoned with him: "You forget your families and would break through heavy encirclement to guard the emperor out—that is truly loyal and righteous.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang's words turned abusive toward Sun Fu, Lu Haowen reasoned with him: "You men forget your families and would cut through the siege to escort the emperor to safety—that is genuine loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然乘輿將駕，必甲乘無闕而後動，詎可輕邪？」

translations.literal: But when the imperial carriage is about to move, armor and mounts must be complete before setting out—how can that be treated lightly?"
translations.idiomatic: But when the imperial carriage is to depart, armor and mounts must be fully ready before it moves—surely that cannot be rushed?"

sentences.zh: 宣詘服曰：「尚書真知軍情。」

translations.literal: Jiang, subdued, said: "Minister, you truly know military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, chastened, said, "Minister, you truly understand military affairs."

sentences.zh: 麾其徒退。

translations.literal: He waved his men back.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 帝再幸金營，好問實從，帝既留，遣好問還，尉拊都城。

translations.literal: The emperor went twice to the Jurchen camp; Haowen actually accompanied him; once the emperor was detained, he sent Haowen back to comfort and reassure the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the Jurchen camp twice; Lu Haowen went with him; when the emperor was detained, he sent Lu Haowen back to pacify the capital.

sentences.zh: 已而金人立張邦昌，以好問為事務官。

translations.literal: Soon the Jurchens set up Zhang Bangchang and appointed Haowen as an administrative officer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jurchens installed Zhang Bangchang and made Lu Haowen one of his administrative officers.

sentences.zh: 邦昌入居都省，好問曰：「相公真欲立邪，抑姑塞敵意而徐為之圖爾？」

translations.literal: Bangchang moved into the chief secretariat; Haowen said: "Sir, do you truly wish to reign—or are you only placating the enemy for now and plotting something else?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang took up residence in the chief secretariat, Lu Haowen asked, "Do you truly mean to reign, or are you merely appeasing the enemy for the moment while you plan something else?"

sentences.zh: 邦昌曰：「是何言也？」

translations.literal: Bangchang said: "What sort of talk is that?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang replied, "What kind of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 好問曰：「相公知中國人情所向乎？

translations.literal: Haowen said: "Do you know where the hearts of the people of China lie?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen said, "Do you know where the hearts of the Chinese people truly lie?

sentences.zh: 特畏女真兵威耳。

translations.literal: They fear only the military might of the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: They submit only because they fear Jurchen military power.

sentences.zh: 女真既去，能保如今日乎？

translations.literal: Once the Jurchens leave, can you hold today's position?
translations.idiomatic: Once the Jurchens are gone, can you keep what you hold today?

sentences.zh: 大元帥在外，元祐皇太后在內，此殆天意，盍亟還政，可轉禍為福。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal is outside; the Yuanyou Empress Dowager is within—this is likely Heaven's intent. Why not quickly return power? Misfortune can be turned to fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal is abroad and the Yuanyou Empress Dowager is within the palace—this may well be Heaven's design. Why not restore power at once and turn disaster into blessing?

sentences.zh: 且省中非人臣所處，宜寓直殿廬，毋令衛士俠陛。

translations.literal: Besides, the chief secretariat is no place for a subject; you should lodge in the hall quarters on duty and not let guards stand beside the throne steps.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the chief secretariat is not where a subject should dwell; you ought to keep temporary quarters in the palace offices and not let armed guards stand at the imperial dais.

sentences.zh: 敵所遺袍帶，非戎人在旁，弛勿服。

translations.literal: The robe and belt the enemy gave you—unless Jurchen soldiers are present, do not wear them loosely.
translations.idiomatic: As for the robe and belt the enemy bestowed on you, do not put them on casually unless Jurchen soldiers are present.

sentences.zh: 車駕未還，所下文書，不當稱聖旨。」

translations.literal: The imperial carriage has not returned; documents you issue should not be called sacred edicts."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has not yet returned; the documents you issue should not be styled imperial edicts."

sentences.zh: 以好問攝門下省。

translations.literal: Haowen was assigned to act as head of the Gate Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen was put in charge of the Gate Palace Secretariat on an acting basis.

sentences.zh: 好問既系銜，仍行舊職。

translations.literal: Though Haowen held this additional title, he still performed his old duties.
translations.idiomatic: Even after receiving this added title, he continued to carry out his former responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 時邦昌雖不改元，而百司文移，必去年號，獨好問所行文書，稱「靖康二年」。

translations.literal: Though Bangchang did not change the reign era, all offices stripped the era name from documents—only Haowen's documents read "the second year of Jingkang."
translations.idiomatic: Although Zhang Bangchang did not change the reign title, every office removed the era name from its documents—only Lu Haowen's papers still read "the second year of Jingkang."

sentences.zh: 吳幵、莫儔請邦昌見金使於紫宸、垂拱殿，好問曰：「宮省故吏驟見禦正衛，必將憤駭，變且不測，奈何？」

translations.literal: Wu Kai and Mo Chou asked Bangchang to receive the Jurchen envoys in the Zichen and Chuigong halls; Haowen said: "Old officials of the palace who suddenly see the Imperial Regalia Guard will surely be outraged; trouble may arise unpredictably—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kai and Mo Chou wanted Zhang Bangchang to receive the Jurchen envoys in the Zichen and Chuigong halls; Lu Haowen objected, "Former palace officials who suddenly see the Imperial Regalia Guard in the audience hall will be enraged; unrest may erupt without warning—what then?"

sentences.zh: 邦昌矍然止。

translations.literal: Bangchang started in alarm and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang, startled, abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 王時雍議肆赦，好問曰：「四壁之外，皆非我有，將誰赦？」

translations.literal: Wang Shiyong proposed a general amnesty; Haowen said: "Beyond the four walls, nothing is ours—whom would we amnesty?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shiyong proposed a general amnesty, Lu Haowen said, "Outside these four walls nothing belongs to us—whom are we to pardon?"

sentences.zh: 乃先赦城中。

translations.literal: They first amnestied those within the city.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore granted amnesty only within the city first.

sentences.zh: 始，金人謀以五千騎取康王，好問聞，即遣人以書白王，言：「大王之兵，度能擊則邀擊之，不然，即宜遠避。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jurchens planned to take Prince Kang with five thousand cavalry; on hearing this, Haowen immediately sent a man with a letter informing the prince: "If Your Highness's forces can strike, intercept them; if not, you should withdraw far away."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jurchens had planned to seize the Prince of Kang with five thousand horsemen; when Lu Haowen learned of it, he at once sent a messenger with a letter telling the prince, "If your forces can engage them, intercept; if not, withdraw to a safe distance."

sentences.zh: 且言：「大王若不自立，恐有不當立而立者。」

translations.literal: He also said: "If Your Highness does not establish yourself, I fear someone unfit to rule may be set up."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If you do not take the throne yourself, I fear someone unworthy may be put in your place."

sentences.zh: 既，又語邦昌曰：「天命人心，皆歸大元帥，相公先遣人推戴，則功無在相公右者。

translations.literal: Later he told Bangchang: "Heaven's mandate and popular sentiment both belong to the Grand Marshal; if you are first to send men urging his accession, no one's merit will surpass yours.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Zhang Bangchang, "Heaven's mandate and the people's hearts both belong to the Grand Marshal; if you are the first to send men urging his enthronement, no one's achievement will exceed yours.

sentences.zh: 若撫機不發，他人聲義致討，悔可追邪？」

translations.literal: If you hesitate and miss the moment, and others raise righteous cause against you, can regret be undone?"
translations.idiomatic: If you let the moment pass and others rise in righteous protest against you, will regret avail you then?"

sentences.zh: 於是邦昌謀遣謝克家奉傳國寶往大元帥府，須金人退乃發。

translations.literal: Bangchang then planned to send Xie Kejia bearing the imperial heirlooms to the Grand Marshal's headquarters, to be dispatched only after the Jurchens withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bangchang then planned to send Xie Kejia with the imperial seal and regalia to the Grand Marshal's headquarters, to be dispatched only after the Jurchens had withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 金將將還，議留兵以衛邦昌。

translations.literal: The Jurchen generals, about to return, debated leaving troops to guard Bangchang.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jurchen commanders prepared to withdraw, they debated leaving soldiers behind to protect Zhang Bangchang.

sentences.zh: 好問曰：「南北異宜，恐北兵不習風土，必不相安。」

translations.literal: Haowen said: "North and south differ in what suits them; I fear northern soldiers unaccustomed to the climate will not settle in peace."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen said, "North and south differ in climate and custom; northern troops unused to the south will not live at ease here."

sentences.zh: 金人曰：「留一勃堇統之可也。」

translations.literal: The Jurchens said: "Leaving one bianjin to command them would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens replied, "It would be enough to leave one bianjin in command."

sentences.zh: 好問曰：「勃堇貴人，有如觸發致疾，則負罪益深。」

translations.literal: Haowen said: "A bianjin is a man of rank; if illness were somehow triggered, the blame would run even deeper."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen said, "A bianjin is a man of high standing; if he fell ill here, the guilt would be all the greater."

sentences.zh: 乃不復留兵。

translations.literal: They therefore left no troops behind.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens therefore decided not to leave any troops behind.

sentences.zh: 金人既行，好問趣遣使詣大元帥府勸進，請元祐太后垂簾，邦昌易服歸太宰位。

translations.literal: Once the Jurchens had gone, Haowen urgently sent envoys to the Grand Marshal's headquarters to urge accession, asked the Yuanyou Empress Dowager to rule from behind the curtain, and had Bangchang change robes and return to his post as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens departed, Lu Haowen hastily sent envoys to the Grand Marshal urging him to take the throne, asked the Yuanyou Empress Dowager to assume the regency, and had Zhang Bangchang change out of imperial garb and resume his post as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太后自延福宮入聽政。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager entered from Yanfu Palace to hear affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager moved from Yanfu Palace to the throne room to conduct affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，太后遣好問奉手書詣行在所，高宗勞之曰：「宗廟獲全，卿之力也。」

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, the Empress Dowager sent Haowen with a personal letter to the mobile court; Gaozong consoled him: "The ancestral temples were preserved—through your strength."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong ascended the throne, the Empress Dowager sent Lu Haowen with a personal letter to the temporary court; Gaozong praised him, saying, "That the ancestral temples survived is your doing."

sentences.zh: 除尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丞相李綱以群臣在圍城中不能執節，欲悉按其罪。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Li Gang, because the officials in the besieged city had failed to hold to integrity, wished to investigate and punish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Li Gang, believing that officials who had remained in the besieged capital had failed to uphold their integrity, wanted to prosecute them all.

sentences.zh: 好問曰：「王業艱難，政宜含垢，繩以峻法，懼者眾矣。」

translations.literal: Haowen said: "Founding the royal enterprise is arduous; it is proper to swallow old grievances; apply harsh law and many will fear."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen replied, "The founding of a dynasty is hard-won; this is a time to bear old stains; tighten the law now and you will frighten too many men."

sentences.zh: 侍御史王賓論好問嘗汙偽命，不可以立新朝。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Attendant Censor Wang Bin argued that Haowen had once been tainted by a false commission and could not serve the new court.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Attendant Censor Wang Bin charged that Lu Haowen had once accepted a usurper's appointment and was unfit to serve the new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「邦昌僭號之初，好問募人齎白書，具道京師內外之事。

translations.literal: Gaozong said: "At the start of Bangchang's usurpation, Haowen recruited men to carry an unsealed letter detailing affairs inside and outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong said, "At the outset of Zhang Bangchang's usurpation, Lu Haowen sent men bearing an open letter describing conditions inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 金人甫退，又遣人勸進。

translations.literal: As soon as the Jurchens withdrew, he again sent men urging my accession.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the Jurchens withdrew, he again sent men urging me to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 考其心跡，非他人比。」

translations.literal: Weighing his heart and conduct, he is not to be compared with others."
translations.idiomatic: Judging his intentions and actions, he stands apart from the others."

sentences.zh: 好問自慚，力求去，且言：「邦昌僭號之時，臣若閉門潔身，實不為難。

translations.literal: Haowen, ashamed, strongly asked to leave and said: "During Bangchang's usurpation, if I had shut my gates and kept myself clean, that would truly have been no hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Lu Haowen pressed hard to resign and wrote, "During Zhang Bangchang's usurpation, had I simply shut my doors and kept myself unstained, that would truly have been easy.

sentences.zh: 徒以世被國恩，所以受賢者之責，冒圍齎書于陛下。」

translations.literal: Only because my family has received the state's grace for generations did I accept wise men's reproach and break through the encirclement to bring a letter to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Only because my family has enjoyed the state's favor for generations did I heed the rebuke of the worthy and risk the siege to deliver a letter to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 疏入，除資政殿學士、知宣州、提舉洞霄宮，以恩封東萊郡侯。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, he was made Academician of the Hall for Administration of State Affairs, Prefect of Xuanzhou, and Supervisor of the Tongxiao Palace; by grace he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Donglai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorial arrived, he was made Academician of the Hall for Administration of State Affairs, Prefect of Xuanzhou, and Supervisor of the Tongxiao Palace, and by special grace was enfeoffed as Marquis of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 避地，卒于桂州。

translations.literal: Seeking refuge, he died in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: While living in exile he died at Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 子本中、揆中、弸中、用中、忱中。

translations.literal: His sons were Benzhong, Kuizhong, Pengzhong, Yongzhong, and Chenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Lu Benzhong, Lu Kuizhong, Lu Pengzhong, Lu Yongzhong, and Lu Chenzhong.

sentences.zh: 孫祖謙、祖儉。

translations.literal: His grandsons were Zu Qian and Zu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons were Lu Zu Qian and Lu Zu Jian.

sentences.zh: 本中、祖謙、祖儉別有傳。

translations.literal: Benzhong, Zu Qian, and Zu Jian have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Benzhong, Lu Zu Qian, and Lu Zu Jian are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 論曰：朱勝非、呂頤浩處苗、劉之變，或巽用其智，或震奮其威，其於復辟討賊之功，固有可言矣。

translations.literal: Commentary: In handling the Miao–Liu mutiny, Zhu Shengfei and Lu Yihao—one yielding and deploying his wit, the other rousing and exerting his authority—both had achievements in restoring the throne and punishing the rebels that deserve mention.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In the Miao–Liu crisis, Zhu Shengfei and Lu Yihao—one supple in the use of intelligence, the other fierce in the exercise of authority—both had real merit in restoring the emperor and punishing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 然李綱、趙鼎當世之所謂賢者，而勝非、頤浩視之若冰炭然，其中之所存，果何如哉。

translations.literal: Yet Li Gang and Zhao Ding were called the worthies of the age, while Shengfei and Yihao treated them like ice and fire—what was truly in their hearts, one wonders?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Gang and Zhao Ding were regarded as the great men of their day, while Shengfei and Yihao treated them like mortal enemies—what, then, was really in their hearts?

sentences.zh: 范宗尹忍于汙張邦昌之偽命，而誣李綱以震主之威，何其繆於是非也。

translations.literal: Fan Zongyin stooped to accept Zhang Bangchang's false commission, yet slandered Li Gang to alarm the ruler with his authority—how perverse his sense of right and wrong!
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zongyin was willing to accept Zhang Bangchang's usurper's commission, yet smeared Li Gang to intimidate the throne—how twisted his judgment of right and wrong!

sentences.zh: 範致虛佞附權臣，大誼已失，其總勤王之師，輕而寡謀，以底於敗，宜哉。

translations.literal: Fan Zhixu fawned on powerful ministers and had already lost great principle; that he should gather the armies that came to rescue the throne yet act lightly and with little planning, ending in defeat—that was only to be expected.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu flattered the mighty and had already forfeited the larger moral claim; that he commanded the relief armies yet acted rashly and without strategy, ending in ruin—that was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 若呂好問處艱難之際，其跡與宗尹同，而屈己就事，以規興復，亦若勝非之處苗、劉，其心有足亮雲。

translations.literal: As for Lu Haowen, in times of hardship his course resembled Zongyin's, yet he humbled himself to take up the work and plan restoration—much as Shengfei in the Miao–Liu affair; his heart has merit enough to be judged clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Haowen, in the same desperate hour, walked a path outwardly like Fan Zongyin's, yet lowered himself to practical work in the hope of restoration—much as Zhu Shengfei had in the Miao–Liu affair; on that score his intentions stand clear enough to be judged favorably.
